#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch Othello Player in development mode:  bash launch.sh
# (--check only verifies the prerequisites and exits.)
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Pick up toolchains installed by rustup and nvm, which only add themselves to
# interactive shells' PATH.
[ -d "$HOME/.cargo/bin" ] && export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -s "$HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  . "$HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh"
fi

missing=0
need() { # need <command> <how to get it>
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Missing: $1. $2" >&2
    missing=1
  fi
}
need cargo "Install Rust: https://rustup.rs"
need node "Install Node.js (an LTS release), e.g. with nvm: https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm"
need npm "It comes with Node.js."
[ "$missing" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
  echo "OK: cargo $(cargo --version | cut -d' ' -f2), node $(node --version), npm $(npm --version)"
  exit 0
fi

if [ ! -d "$ROOT/ui/node_modules" ]; then
  echo "Installing UI dependencies (first run)..."
  (cd "$ROOT/ui" && npm install)
fi

# The first launch compiles the Rust side and takes a minute or two.
cd "$ROOT/app"
exec npx --prefix ../ui tauri dev

/* Othello Player — casino night.
   Polished wood, black & white discs, disco-pop neon. All motion respects the
   in-app "Animations" setting (data-motion="off") and prefers-reduced-motion. */

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;

  /* neon / disco lights */
  --pink: #ff2fb3;
  --cyan: #1de9ff;
  --yellow: #ffd23f;
  --purple: #8a3dff;
  --lime: #7cff4a;

  /* room */
  --room: #0b0614;
  --room-glow: #1a0b33;
  --ink: #f6efe6;
  --ink-dim: #b9aecb;

  /* wood */
  --walnut-dark: #2c170c;
  --walnut: #4a2a17;
  --walnut-light: #6b3f22;
  --oak: #c58d52;
  --maple: #e2b97e;
  --groove: #3a2210;
  --brass: #e8c170;

  --font-display: 'Monoton', 'Impact', sans-serif;
  --font-serif: 'Playfair Display', 'Didot', 'Bodoni MT', Georgia, serif;
  --font-ui: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;

  font-family: var(--font-ui);
}

/* Daylight variant: a brighter room, same wood and lights. */
:root[data-theme='light'] {
  color-scheme: light;
  --room: #f3e9f7;
  --room-glow: #ffd9f0;
  --ink: #26122f;
  --ink-dim: #5d4a6b;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {
  :root:not([data-theme]) {
    color-scheme: light;
    --room: #f3e9f7;
    --room-glow: #ffd9f0;
    --ink: #26122f;
    --ink-dim: #5d4a6b;
  }
}

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

html, body { height: 100%; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--room);
  color: var(--ink);
  overflow-x: hidden;
}

#app { min-height: 100%; }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ shared pieces */

/* Neon text: the colour cycles through the light palette. */
.neon {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-weight: 400;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  color: #fff;
  text-shadow:
    0 0 6px #fff,
    0 0 14px var(--pink),
    0 0 30px var(--pink),
    0 0 60px var(--purple);
  animation: neon-cycle 9s linear infinite, neon-flicker 5s infinite;
}

/* Buttons: glossy black lacquer with a neon edge; .primary is ivory. */
button.btn {
  font-family: var(--font-serif);
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 1.05rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: #fff;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #2e2a33 0%, #0e0c11 55%, #000 100%);
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border-radius: 999px;
  padding: 0.7rem 1.6rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  position: relative;
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35),
    inset 0 -3px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6),
    0 4px 0 #000,
    0 8px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5),
    0 0 14px color-mix(in srgb, var(--pink) 55%, transparent);
  background-clip: padding-box;
  transition: transform 0.12s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease, filter 0.2s ease;
}
button.btn::before {
  /* neon edge */
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: -2px;
  border-radius: inherit;
  z-index: -1;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--pink), var(--cyan), var(--yellow), var(--purple), var(--pink));
  background-size: 300% 100%;
  animation: edge-slide 6s linear infinite;
}
button.btn:hover:not(:disabled) {
  transform: translateY(-2px);
  filter: brightness(1.15);
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4),
    inset 0 -3px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6),
    0 6px 0 #000,
    0 12px 22px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55),
    0 0 26px color-mix(in srgb, var(--cyan) 70%, transparent);
}
button.btn:active:not(:disabled) {
  transform: translateY(3px);
  box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7), 0 1px 0 #000, 0 0 12px var(--pink);
}
button.btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 4px; }
button.btn:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: default; filter: grayscale(0.6); }
button.btn:disabled::before { animation: none; opacity: 0.4; }
button.btn.primary {
  color: #1b0e08;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fffaf0 0%, #f1e3c8 55%, #d9c49b 100%);
  box-shadow:

}

    left: Math.random() * 100,
    delay: Math.random() * 1.8,
    duration: 3 + Math.random() * 2.5,
    color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length],
    size: 7 + Math.random() * 8,
    spin: (Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * (360 + Math.random() * 720),
    drift: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 30
  }));
</script>

<!-- The board: walnut frame with chasing marquee bulbs, oak squares, glossy 3D discs.
     It only renders the snapshot it is given; all rules live in the engine. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { squareName, type Snapshot } from './api';

  let {
    snap,
    showLegal,
    hintSquare,
    onSquare
  }: {
    snap: Snapshot;
    showLegal: boolean;
    hintSquare: number | null;
    onSquare: (square: number) => void;
  } = $props();

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => i);

  // Flips ripple outward from the placed disc: delay grows with distance.
  function flipDelay(i: number): number {
    if (snap.last_move === null || !snap.flipped.includes(i)) return 0;
    const dr = Math.abs(Math.floor(i / 8) - Math.floor(snap.last_move / 8));
    const dc = Math.abs((i % 8) - (snap.last_move % 8));
    return 120 + (Math.max(dr, dc) - 1) * 130;
  }

  const describe = (i: number, cell: number) =>
    `${squareName(i)}${cell === 1 ? ', black' : cell === 2 ? ', white' : ', empty'}`;
</script>

<div class="frame">
  <div class="bulbs top"><i class="a"></i><i class="b"></i></div>
  <div class="bulbs bottom"><i class="a"></i><i class="b"></i></div>
  <div class="bulbs left"><i class="a"></i><i class="b"></i></div>
  <div class="bulbs right"><i class="a"></i><i class="b"></i></div>

  <div class="board" role="grid" aria-label="Othello board">
    {#each cells as i (i)}
      {@const cell = snap.board[i]}
      {@const legal = snap.legal.includes(i)}
      {@const flipped = snap.flipped.includes(i)}
      <button
        class="cell"
        class:alt={(Math.floor(i / 8) + i) % 2 === 1}
        class:last={snap.last_move === i}
        class:legal={legal}
        class:hint={hintSquare === i}
        class:flipped
        disabled={!legal}
        onclick={() => onSquare(i)}
        aria-label={describe(i, cell)}
      >
        {#if cell !== 0}
          <span class="lift">
            <span class="disc" class:white={cell === 2} style:--delay="{flipDelay(i)}ms">
              <span class="face b"></span>
              <span class="face w"></span>
            </span>
          </span>
        {:else if legal && showLegal}
          <span class="ring"></span>
        {/if}
        {#if snap.last_move === i}<span class="marker"></span>{/if}
      </button>
    {/each}
  </div>
</div>

# Design tokens

This file **drives the look of the app**. Edit a value, save, and the app reloads
with it (in `bash launch.sh` dev mode). No code changes needed.

## How to edit

- Every line inside a `tokens` block is `name: value`. The value is plain CSS: a colour,
  a gradient, a length (`26px`, `38px`), a time (`0.6s`, `130ms`), a percentage, a font stack.
- Text after ` # ` (a space, `#`, a space) on a line is a comment. A colour like `#ff2fb3`
  is not a comment because no space follows its `#`.
- A value can reuse another token with `var(--d-the-name)`: underscores in a token name become
  hyphens, e.g. `neon_pink` is `var(--d-neon-pink)`. That is how the lights propagate: change
  `neon_pink` once and every pink glow follows.
- Don't rename or delete tokens: the app reads them by name. The build fails if the code uses a
  token that is missing here, and warns if a token here is not used by anything.
- Colours with transparency: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`. Gradients: `linear-gradient(...)`,
  `radial-gradient(...)`; multi-layer values separate layers with commas.
- Speeds are durations: **bigger = slower**. To make something static, set a huge duration
  (`9999s`). To switch all motion off, use Settings > Animations in the app.

Sections follow the screen from the outside in: the room, text, buttons, option boxes,
scoreboard, board frame, bulbs, board surface, discs, animations, hints, dialogs.

---

## 1. Neon lights (the shared palette)

Used everywhere: background glows, beams, neon text, button edges, hints, bulbs, confetti.

```tokens
neon_pink: #ff2fb3
neon_cyan: #1de9ff
neon_yellow: #ffd23f
neon_purple: #8a3dff

```

## 2. Room (main_bg: the page behind everything)

```tokens

beams_opacity: 0.55                       # rotating disco spotlight beams: 0 = off, 1 = strong
beams_spin_duration: 70s                  # one full turn of the beams (bigger = slower)
blobs_opacity: 0.55                       # the big drifting colour glows: 0 = off
blobs_blur: 70px                          # how soft the glows are
blobs_drift_slowness: 1                   # multiplier on drift time: 2 = twice as slow, 0.5 = twice as fast
```

```tokens

font_serif: 'Playfair Display', 'Didot', 'Bodoni MT', Georgia, serif                 # buttons, labels, numbers
```

cat tsconfig.node.json; cat > design-plugin.ts <<'EOF'
// Turns ../design.md into CSS variables (--d-<token-name>) injected into index.html,
// reloads the dev server when the file changes, and checks that tokens and code agree.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { Plugin } from 'vite';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const DESIGN_FILE = resolve(here, '../design.md');
const SRC_DIR = resolve(here, 'src');

/** Parse the ```tokens blocks of design.md into [name, value] pairs. */
export function parseTokens(markdown: string): Map<string, string> {
  const tokens = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const block of markdown.matchAll(/```tokens\n([\s\S]*?)```/g)) {
    for (const [i, raw] of block[1].split('\n').entries()) {
      const line = raw.trim();
      if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) continue;
      const colon = line.indexOf(':');
      const name = colon > 0 ? line.slice(0, colon).trim() : '';
      if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/.test(name)) {
        throw new Error(`design.md: cannot read token line "${line}" (block line ${i + 1}); expected "name: value"`);
      }
      // A comment starts at " # " (hash followed by a space); "#ff2fb3" is a colour.
      const value = line.slice(colon + 1).split(/\s+#\s/)[0].trim();
      if (!value) throw new Error(`design.md: token "${name}" has no value`);
      if (tokens.has(name)) throw new Error(`design.md: token "${name}" is defined twice`);
      tokens.set(name, value);
    }
  }
  return tokens;
}

const cssName = (token: string) => `--d-${token.replace(/_/g, '-')}`;

function sourceFiles(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = join(dir, entry);
    return statSync(path).isDirectory() ? sourceFiles(path) : /\.(css|svelte|ts)$/.test(entry) ? [path] : [];
  });
}

/** Every --d-* variable the code (or another token) refers to. */
function usedVariables(tokens: Map<string, string>): Set<string> {
  const used = new Set<string>();
  const scan = (text: string) => text.match(/--d-[a-z0-9-]+/g)?.forEach((v) => used.add(v));
  sourceFiles(SRC_DIR).forEach((f) => scan(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')));
  tokens.forEach((value) => scan(value));
  return used;
}

function load(warn: (msg: string) => void): string {
  const tokens = parseTokens(readFileSync(DESIGN_FILE, 'utf8'));
  const defined = new Set([...tokens.keys()].map(cssName));
  const used = usedVariables(tokens);
  const missing = [...used].filter((v) => !defined.has(v));
  if (missing.length) {
    throw new Error(`design.md is missing tokens the app uses: ${missing.map((v) => v.slice(4).replace(/-/g, '_')).join(', ')}`);
  }
  const unused = [...defined].filter((v) => !used.has(v));
  if (unused.length) warn(`design.md has tokens nothing uses: ${unused.map((v) => v.slice(4).replace(/-/g, '_')).join(', ')}`);
  const lines = [...tokens].map(([name, value]) => `  ${cssName(name)}: ${value};`);
  return `:root {\n${lines.join('\n')}\n}`;
}

export default function design(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: 'othello-design',
    buildStart() {
      load((m) => this.warn(m)); // fail the build early on a bad design.md
    },
    configureServer(server) {
      server.watcher.add(DESIGN_FILE);
      server.watcher.on('change', (file) => {
        if (resolve(file) === DESIGN_FILE) {
          server.config.logger.info('design.md changed, reloading', { timestamp: true });
          server.ws.send({ type: 'full-reload' });
        }
      });
    },
    transformIndexHtml: {
      order: 'pre',
      handler() {
        const css = load((m) => console.warn(`\n[design] ${m}`));
        return [{ tag: 'style', attrs: { id: 'design-tokens' }, children: css, injectTo: 'head-prepend' }];
      }
    }
  };
}

sed -i "s#from './design-plugin'#from './design-plugin.ts'#" vite.config.ts && cat > src/app.css <<'EOF'
/* Othello Player: casino night.
   Every colour, texture and timing comes from a design token (--d-*) defined in the
   repo-root design.md and injected by design-plugin.ts. Edit design.md, not this file,
   to tune the look. Motion respects Settings > Animations (data-motion="off") and
   prefers-reduced-motion. */

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  font-family: var(--d-font-ui);
}

/* The room is a night casino by default (whatever the OS theme). Light is an explicit
   opt-in in Settings: a brighter room, same wood and lights. */
:root[data-theme='light'] {
  color-scheme: light;
  --d-main-bg: var(--d-daylight-main-bg);
  --d-main-bg-glow: var(--d-daylight-main-bg-glow);
  --d-ink: var(--d-daylight-ink);
  --d-ink-dim: var(--d-daylight-ink-dim);
}

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

html, body { height: 100%; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--d-main-bg);
  color: var(--d-ink);
  overflow-x: hidden;
}

#app { min-height: 100%; }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ shared pieces */

  // CSS turns it into a delay using the timings in design.md (section 12).
  function ring(i: number): number {
    if (snap.last_move === null || !snap.flipped.includes(i)) return 0;
    const dr = Math.abs(Math.floor(i / 8) - Math.floor(snap.last_move / 8));
    const dc = Math.abs((i % 8) - (snap.last_move % 8));
    return Math.max(dr, dc) - 1;
  }

Bash: Teach the design plugin about per-mode token blocks
cd /home/palak_raisinghani/my/courses/Othello-Player/ui && python3 - <<'EOF'
p="design-plugin.ts"; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("/** Parse the ```tokens"); b=s.index("const cssName")
s=s[:a]+'''export type Tokens = Map<string, string>;

/** UI modes. `casino` is the base block (full set); the others list only overrides. */
export const MODES = ['casino', 'cafe'] as const;

function parseBlock(body: string, label: string): Tokens {
  const tokens: Tokens = new Map();
  for (const [i, raw] of body.split('\\n').entries()) {
    const line = raw.trim();
    if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) continue;
    const colon = line.indexOf(':');
    const name = colon > 0 ? line.slice(0, colon).trim() : '';
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/.test(name)) {
      throw new Error(`design.md (${label}): cannot read token line "${line}" (block line ${i + 1}); expected "name: value"`);
    }
    // A comment starts at " # " (hash followed by a space); "#ff2fb3" is a colour.
    const value = line.slice(colon + 1).split(/\\s+#\\s/)[0].trim();
    if (!value) throw new Error(`design.md (${label}): token "${name}" has no value`);
    if (tokens.has(name)) throw new Error(`design.md (${label}): token "${name}" is defined twice`);
    tokens.set(name, value);
  }
  return tokens;
}

/**
 * Parse design.md. A ```tokens block is the Casino base (every token); a ```tokens cafe
 * block overrides some of them for Cafe mode. Several blocks of the same mode are merged.
 */
export function parseDesign(markdown: string): Record<(typeof MODES)[number], Tokens> {
  const modes = { casino: new Map(), cafe: new Map() } as Record<(typeof MODES)[number], Tokens>;
  for (const m of markdown.matchAll(/```tokens(?:[ \\t]+([a-z]+))?\\n([\\s\\S]*?)```/g)) {
    const mode = (m[1] ?? 'casino') as (typeof MODES)[number];
    if (!MODES.includes(mode)) throw new Error(`design.md: unknown UI mode "${m[1]}" (known: ${MODES.join(', ')})`);
    for (const [name, value] of parseBlock(m[2], mode)) {
      if (modes[mode].has(name)) throw new Error(`design.md (${mode}): token "${name}" is defined twice`);
      modes[mode].set(name, value);
    }
  }
  return modes;
}

'''+s[b:]
a=s.index("/** Every --d-* variable"); b=s.index("export default function design")
s=s[:a]+'''/** Every --d-* variable the code (or a token value) refers to. */
function usedVariables(all: Tokens[]): Set<string> {
  const used = new Set<string>();
  const scan = (text: string) => text.match(/--d-[a-z0-9-]+/g)?.forEach((v) => used.add(v));
  sourceFiles(SRC_DIR).forEach((f) => scan(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')));
  all.forEach((tokens) => tokens.forEach((value) => scan(value)));
  return used;
}

const human = (cssVar: string) => cssVar.slice(4).replace(/-/g, '_');

function load(warn: (msg: string) => void): string {
  const { casino, cafe } = parseDesign(readFileSync(DESIGN_FILE, 'utf8'));
  const defined = new Set([...casino.keys()].map(cssName));
  const used = usedVariables([casino, cafe]);

  const missing = [...used].filter((v) => !defined.has(v));
  if (missing.length) throw new Error(`design.md is missing tokens the app uses: ${missing.map(human).join(', ')}`);

  const stray = [...cafe.keys()].filter((k) => !casino.has(k));
  if (stray.length) throw new Error(`design.md: the cafe block overrides tokens that do not exist: ${stray.join(', ')}`);

  const unused = [...defined].filter((v) => !used.has(v));
  if (unused.length) warn(`design.md has tokens nothing uses: ${unused.map(human).join(', ')}`);

  const rule = (selector: string, tokens: Tokens) =>
    `${selector} {\\n${[...tokens].map(([n, v]) => `  ${cssName(n)}: ${v};`).join('\\n')}\\n}`;
  return `${rule(':root', casino)}\\n${rule(":root[data-ui-mode='cafe']", cafe)}`;
}

'''+s[b:]
open(p,"w").write(s)

The casino styling, the new design.md, and Casino and Cafe UI modes are all committed (4682e55). I checked the looks through headless-Firefox screenshots of the UI, not by playing in the app window. I haven't tried clicking through a real game with the new styling, or the live reload, in the Tauri window itself.

Verification: the 40 Rust tests pass, clippy is clean, and the UI type-checks and builds.

Casino mode (default)

  • Room: a dark room with drifting colour glows and slow rotating disco beams.
  • Title: a flickering neon sign in Monoton, installed locally so the app stays offline.
  • Buttons: black lacquer with colour-cycling neon edges, plus an ivory main button.
  • Board: a walnut frame with chasing marquee bulbs, oak and maple squares, and glossy black and white discs.
  • Disc animations: discs drop in and flips ripple outward from the new disc, rising as they turn.
  • Hints and highlights: pulsing rings mark playable squares, and a frame marks the last move.
  • Win screen: confetti appears on a win, but not when you lose to the computer.

Cafe mode (new)

You didn't describe Cafe, so I chose a look: a cream latte room, serif lettering, ceramic and espresso buttons, a light oak board, slow string lights and gentler animation. It has no beams or neon flicker. Switch styles in Settings > Style, or with the switch on the home screen.

design.md

  • Tokens: it holds every tunable value, including the fields you asked for (main background, option boxes, board frame and border, squares, discs, flip animations).
  • Casino and Cafe blocks: the Casino blocks define all of them, and the Cafe block lists only what differs. Add a line to the Cafe block to make it differ in another way.
  • Live reload: edit a value, save, and the running app reloads.
  • Checks: a missing token fails the build and names it, a stray token in the Cafe block fails, a malformed line fails with the line shown, and an unused token warns. I tested each case.

Decision for you

I replaced the Light/Dark/System theme setting with Casino/Cafe, because Cafe is the bright look and keeping both conflicted. Settings files from before still load.

Known issues

  • Corner bulbs: the marquee bulbs leave small partial bulbs at the frame corners, most visible in Cafe.
  • Sound: the sound setting still does nothing.
  • Reload test: my first live-reload attempt, which swapped the neon palette in design.md and re-screenshotted, failed because Firefox didn't save the capture. The build checks and the Cafe overrides prove the token system works, but I never captured that exact before-and-after, so try editing a value yourself.
  • Dev server: your app's dev server is still running with the new build. I removed my temporary preview files and screenshot folders.

// Turns ../design.md into CSS variables (--d-<token-name>) injected into index.html,
// reloads the dev server when the file changes, and checks that tokens and code agree.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { Plugin } from 'vite';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const DESIGN_FILE = resolve(here, '../design.md');
const SRC_DIR = resolve(here, 'src');

export type Tokens = Map<string, string>;

/** Parse the ```tokens blocks of design.md into [name, value] pairs. */
export function parseDesign(markdown: string): Tokens {
  const tokens: Tokens = new Map();
  for (const block of markdown.matchAll(/```tokens\n([\s\S]*?)```/g)) {
    for (const [i, raw] of block[1].split('\n').entries()) {
      const line = raw.trim();
      if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) continue;
      const colon = line.indexOf(':');
      const name = colon > 0 ? line.slice(0, colon).trim() : '';
      if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/.test(name)) {
        throw new Error(`design.md: cannot read token line "${line}" (block line ${i + 1}); expected "name: value"`);
      }
      // A comment starts at " # " (hash followed by a space); "#ff2fb3" is a colour.
      const value = line.slice(colon + 1).split(/\s+#\s/)[0].trim();
      if (!value) throw new Error(`design.md: token "${name}" has no value`);
      if (tokens.has(name)) throw new Error(`design.md: token "${name}" is defined twice`);
      tokens.set(name, value);
    }
  }
  return tokens;
}

const cssName = (token: string) => `--d-${token.replace(/_/g, '-')}`;
const human = (cssVar: string) => cssVar.slice(4).replace(/-/g, '_');

function sourceFiles(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = join(dir, entry);
    return statSync(path).isDirectory() ? sourceFiles(path) : /\.(css|svelte|ts)$/.test(entry) ? [path] : [];
  });
}

/** Every --d-* variable the code (or another token) refers to. */
function usedVariables(tokens: Tokens): Set<string> {
  const used = new Set<string>();
  const scan = (text: string) => text.match(/--d-[a-z0-9-]+/g)?.forEach((v) => used.add(v));
  sourceFiles(SRC_DIR).forEach((f) => scan(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')));
  tokens.forEach((value) => scan(value));
  return used;
}

function load(warn: (msg: string) => void): string {
  const tokens = parseDesign(readFileSync(DESIGN_FILE, 'utf8'));
  const defined = new Set([...tokens.keys()].map(cssName));
  const used = usedVariables(tokens);
  const missing = [...used].filter((v) => !defined.has(v));
  if (missing.length) throw new Error(`design.md is missing tokens the app uses: ${missing.map(human).join(', ')}`);
  const unused = [...defined].filter((v) => !used.has(v));
  if (unused.length) warn(`design.md has tokens nothing uses: ${unused.map(human).join(', ')}`);
  return `:root {\n${[...tokens].map(([n, v]) => `  ${cssName(n)}: ${v};`).join('\n')}\n}`;
}

# Design tokens

This file **drives the look of the app**. Edit a value, save, and the app reloads
with it (in `bash launch.sh` dev mode). No code changes needed.

The look: a casino card room. Mahogany wood everywhere, burnished brass rims, red velvet
buttons, a green felt board, glossy black and white discs, warm disco-pop lights, and poker
chips that splash across the screen at the start of a game and rain down when someone wins.

## How to edit

- Every line inside a `tokens` block is `name: value`. The value is plain CSS: a colour,
  a gradient, a length (`26px`, `38px`), a time (`0.6s`, `130ms`), a percentage, a font stack,
  or an image (`url(/textures/wood.png) center / cover`).
- Text after ` # ` (a space, `#`, a space) on a line is a comment. A colour like `#ff2fb3`
  is not a comment because no space follows its `#`.
- A value can reuse another token with `var(--d-the-name)`: underscores in a token name become
  hyphens, e.g. `brass_light` is `var(--d-brass-light)`. Change `brass` once and every brass
  edge follows.
- **Textures** live in `ui/public/textures/` (`wood.png`, `red-velvet.png`, `green-velvet.png`).
  To use your own, drop a PNG or JPG there and point a token at it, e.g.
  `url(/textures/my-felt.jpg) center / cover`.
- Don't rename or delete tokens: the app reads them by name. The build fails if the code uses a
  token that is missing here, and warns if a token here is not used by anything.
- Colours with transparency: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`. Multi-layer values (a gradient over a
  texture) separate layers with commas; the first layer is on top.
- Speeds are durations: **bigger = slower**. To make something static, set a huge duration
  (`9999s`). To switch all motion off, use Settings > Animations in the app.

Sections go from the outside in: neon lights, the room, text, brass and velvet, buttons,
icon buttons, option boxes, scoreboard, board frame, bulbs, board surface, discs, disc
animations, hints, banners and dialogs, poker chips, the roulette wheel.

---

## 1. Neon lights (the shared accent palette)

Used for the title sign, hint rings, bulbs, glows and the light washes on the wood.

```tokens
neon_pink: #ff2fb3
neon_cyan: #1de9ff
neon_yellow: #ffd23f
neon_purple: #8a3dff
neon_lime: #7cff4a
```

## 2. Room (main_bg: the wooden wall behind everything)

```tokens
main_bg: #1c0b06                          # colour shown if the image is missing
main_bg_image: url(/textures/wood.png) center / cover     # the mahogany wood
main_bg_tint: rgba(12, 4, 2, 0.5)         # darkens the wood: lower = brighter wood, 0 = untouched
main_bg_glow: rgba(255, 176, 96, 0.28)    # warm lamp light pooling near the top centre
vignette_color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)        # dark edges of the screen (transparent = none)
blobs_opacity: 0.28                       # soft coloured light washes drifting over the wood: 0 = off
blobs_blend: screen                       # how the washes mix with the wood
blobs_blur: 70px
blobs_drift_slowness: 1                   # 2 = half speed, 0.5 = double speed
glint_color: rgba(255, 214, 140, 0.9)     # the golden reflection that sweeps across the wood
glint_opacity: 0.2                        # 0 = off
glint_duration: 16s                       # one sweep (bigger = slower)
```

## 3. Text and fonts

```tokens
ink: #f6ead7                              # main text
ink_dim: #cdb89a                          # secondary text (tagline, history)
font_display: 'Monoton', 'Impact', sans-serif                                        # neon sign lettering
font_serif: 'Playfair Display', 'Didot', 'Bodoni MT', Georgia, serif                 # buttons, labels, numbers
font_ui: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif                    # everything else
```

sign_core: #fff6e0                        # the bright tube colour
sign_glow: var(--d-neon-pink)             # near glow

/* Othello Player: a casino card room.
   Every colour, texture and timing comes from a design token (--d-*) defined in the
   repo-root design.md and injected by design-plugin.ts. Edit design.md, not this file,
   to tune the look. Motion respects Settings > Animations (data-motion="off") and
   prefers-reduced-motion. */

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  font-family: var(--d-font-ui);
}

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

html, body { height: 100%; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--d-main-bg);
  color: var(--d-ink);
  overflow-x: hidden;
}

#app { min-height: 100%; }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ shared pieces */

/* Neon sign text: the tube colour cycles through the palette and flickers. */
.neon {
  font-family: var(--d-font-display);
  font-weight: var(--d-sign-weight);
  letter-spacing: var(--d-sign-letter-spacing);
  color: var(--d-sign-core);
  text-shadow:
    0 0 6px var(--d-sign-core),
    0 0 14px var(--d-sign-glow),
    0 0 30px var(--d-sign-glow),
    0 0 60px var(--d-sign-glow-far);
  animation:
    neon-cycle var(--d-sign-hue-cycle-duration) linear infinite,
    neon-flicker var(--d-sign-flicker-duration) infinite;
}

/* Buttons: a brass rim (the button's own background) around a red velvet face (::before).
   The face sits behind the label because the button is its own stacking context. */
button.btn {
  --face: var(--d-button-bg);
  --lip: var(--d-button-lip);
  --glow: color-mix(in srgb, var(--d-button-glow) 50%, transparent);
  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;
  font-family: var(--d-font-serif);
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 1.05rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: var(--d-button-text);
  text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7);
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--d-button-radius);
  padding: calc(0.7rem + var(--d-button-rim)) calc(1.6rem + var(--d-button-rim));
  cursor: pointer;
  background: var(--d-brass-gradient);
  background-size: 300% 100%;
  animation: brass-shine var(--d-brass-shine-duration) linear infinite;
  box-shadow:
    0 4px 0 var(--lip),
    0 8px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55),
    0 0 14px var(--glow);
  transition: transform 0.12s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease, filter 0.2s ease;
}

<!-- Start of a game: poker chips are thrown in from the bottom and the sides, arc across the
     screen, land, bounce and fade. Counts, colours, size and timing come from design.md (section 17).
     Calls `ondone` when the last chip has faded so the parent can remove it. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';

  let { ondone }: { ondone?: () => void } = $props();

  const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const COLORS = css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-colors').split(',').map((c) => c.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const COUNT = Math.max(0, Number.parseInt(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-splash-count'), 10) || 0);
  const DURATION = Number.parseFloat(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-splash-duration')) || 2.8; // seconds
  const VALUES = ['5', '10', '25', '50', '100', '500'];
  const MAX_DELAY = 0.7;

  const rand = (min: number, max: number) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);

  // Launch points: bottom-left corner, bottom-centre, bottom-right corner (all just off screen).
  const ORIGINS = [
    { x: -6, y: 104 },
    { x: 50, y: 110 },
    { x: 106, y: 104 }
  ];

  const chips = Array.from({ length: COUNT }, (_, i) => {
    const o = ORIGINS[i % ORIGINS.length];
    const tx = rand(5, 95);
    const ty = rand(10, 88);
    return {
      color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] ?? '#b3202a',
      value: VALUES[i % VALUES.length],
      sx: o.x, sy: o.y,
      mx: (o.x + tx) / 2 + rand(-8, 8),
      my: Math.min(o.y, ty) - rand(14, 32),
      tx, ty,
      r1: rand(-300, 300),
      r2: rand(-540, 540),
      tilt: rand(0, 1) < 0.5 ? -1 : 1,
      delay: (i / Math.max(COUNT, 1)) * MAX_DELAY + rand(0, 0.12),
      scale: rand(0.85, 1.25)
    };
  });

  onMount(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => ondone?.(), (DURATION + MAX_DELAY + 0.4) * 1000);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  });
</script>

<div class="splash" aria-hidden="true">
  {#each chips as c}
    <div
      class="flight"
      style="--sx:{c.sx}vw; --sy:{c.sy}vh; --mx:{c.mx}vw; --my:{c.my}vh; --tx:{c.tx}vw; --ty:{c.ty}vh;
             --r1:{c.r1}deg; --r2:{c.r2}deg; --delay:{c.delay}s; --k:{c.scale}"
    >
      <div class="tumble" style="--tilt:{c.tilt}">
        <span class="pchip" data-v={c.value} style="--c:{c.color}"></span>
      </div>
    </div>
  {/each}
</div>

<style>
  .splash {
    position: fixed;
    inset: 0;
    z-index: 25;
    pointer-events: none;
    overflow: hidden;
    perspective: 700px;
  }
  .flight {
    position: absolute;
    left: 0;
    top: 0;
    margin: calc(var(--d-chip-size) / -2) 0 0 calc(var(--d-chip-size) / -2);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: splash var(--d-chip-splash-duration) cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.6, 0.4, 1) var(--delay) both;
  }
  /* The chip spins edge-over-edge while it is in the air. */
  .tumble {
    transform-style: preserve-3d;
    animation: tumble 0.55s linear var(--delay) 4 both;
  }
  @keyframes splash {
    0% { transform: translate(var(--sx), var(--sy)) scale(0.3) rotate(0deg); opacity: 0; }
    8% { opacity: 1; }
    45% { transform: translate(var(--mx), var(--my)) scale(calc(var(--k) * 1.15)) rotate(var(--r1)); }
    72% { transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty)) scale(var(--k)) rotate(var(--r2)); opacity: 1; }
    80% { transform: translate(var(--tx), calc(var(--ty) - 2.5vh)) scale(var(--k)) rotate(var(--r2)); }
    88% { transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty)) scale(var(--k)) rotate(var(--r2)); opacity: 1; }
    100% { transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty)) scale(var(--k)) rotate(var(--r2)); opacity: 0; }
  }
  @keyframes tumble {
    from { transform: rotateX(0deg); }
    to { transform: rotateX(calc(360deg * var(--tilt))); }
  }
</style>

<!-- Victory: poker chips rain from the top of the screen, tumbling as they fall.
     Counts, colours, size and speed come from design.md (section 17). -->
<script lang="ts">
  const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const COLORS = css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-colors').split(',').map((c) => c.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const COUNT = Math.max(0, Number.parseInt(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-rain-count'), 10) || 0);
  const SLOWNESS = Number.parseFloat(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-rain-slowness')) || 1;
  const VALUES = ['5', '10', '25', '50', '100', '500'];

  const rand = (min: number, max: number) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);

  const chips = Array.from({ length: COUNT }, (_, i) => ({
    color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] ?? '#b3202a',
    value: VALUES[i % VALUES.length],
    left: rand(0, 100),
    delay: rand(0, 2.4),
    duration: rand(2.6, 4.8) * SLOWNESS,
    scale: rand(0.7, 1.2),
    drift: rand(-14, 14),
    spinZ: (Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * rand(180, 720),
    spinX: (Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * rand(360, 1080)
  }));
</script>

<div class="rain" aria-hidden="true">
  {#each chips as c}
    <div
      class="drop"
      style="left:{c.left}%; --delay:{c.delay}s; --dur:{c.duration}s; --k:{c.scale};
             --drift:{c.drift}vw; --sz:{c.spinZ}deg; --sx:{c.spinX}deg"
    >
      <span class="pchip" data-v={c.value} style="--c:{c.color}"></span>
    </div>
  {/each}
</div>

<style>
  .rain {
    position: fixed;
    inset: 0;
    z-index: 25;
    pointer-events: none;
    overflow: hidden;
    perspective: 800px;
  }
  .drop {
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    margin-left: calc(var(--d-chip-size) / -2);
    opacity: 0;
    transform-style: preserve-3d;
    animation: rain var(--dur) cubic-bezier(0.35, 0.05, 0.75, 0.6) var(--delay) infinite;
  }
  @keyframes rain {
    0% { transform: translate3d(0, -14vh, 0) scale(var(--k)) rotateX(0deg) rotateZ(0deg); opacity: 1; }
    92% { opacity: 1; }
    100% { transform: translate3d(var(--drift), 112vh, 0) scale(var(--k)) rotateX(var(--sx)) rotateZ(var(--sz)); opacity: 1; }
  }
</style>

import '@fontsource/monoton'
import '@fontsource/playfair-display/700.css'
import '@fontsource/playfair-display/900.css'
import './app.css'
import { flushSync, mount } from 'svelte'
import App from './App.svelte'

// Temporary design harness: the real App against a fake Tauri backend.
const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const over = q.has('over');
const board: number[] = Array(64).fill(0);
const sq = (n: string) => 'abcdefgh'.indexOf(n[0]) + 8 * (+n[1] - 1);
['d4','e5','c3','d3','e3','c4','f4','d6','e6','c5','d5'].forEach((n, i) => (board[sq(n)] = i % 3 === 0 ? 2 : 1));
['e4','f5','b4','c6','f6'].forEach((n, i) => (board[sq(n)] = i % 2 ? 2 : 1));
const snap = {
  board, to_move: 'black', awaiting: over ? 'nobody' : 'human',
  legal: over ? [] : ['b3','b5','c7','e7','g4','g6','f3','g5'].map(sq),
  last_move: sq('c5'), flipped: [sq('d5')], black_count: 31, white_count: 22,
  status: over ? { state: 'over', winner: 'black', resigned: false } : { state: 'playing' },
  mode: { kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty: 3, human: 'black' }, can_undo: true, ply: 12,
  history: ['d3', 'c3', 'c4', 'e3', 'f4', 'b4', 'c5']
};
const settings = { show_legal_moves: true, animations: !q.has('still'), sound: true, default_difficulty: 2, default_human_side: 'black' };
(window as any).__TAURI_INTERNALS__ = {
  invoke: async (cmd: string) => (cmd === 'get_settings' ? settings : cmd.startsWith('plugin:') ? 1 : snap),
  transformCallback: () => 1
};
// ?freeze=T pauses the chip animations T seconds in (keeping each chip's own stagger).
if (q.has('freeze')) {
  const t = q.get('freeze');
  const st = document.createElement('style');
  st.textContent = `.flight,.tumble,.drop{animation-play-state:paused!important;animation-delay:calc(var(--delay) - ${t}s)!important}`;
  document.head.appendChild(st);
}
mount(App, { target: document.getElementById('app')! });
flushSync();
if (q.has('game') || over) {
  (document.querySelector('.menu .btn') as HTMLElement | null)?.click();
  flushSync();
  (document.querySelector('form') as HTMLFormElement).requestSubmit();
}

p="README.md"; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("## Tuning the look: `design.md`"); b=s.index("## Run the app (development)")
s=s[:a]+"""## Tuning the look: `design.md`

The UI is a casino card room: mahogany wood, burnished brass rims, red velvet buttons, a green felt board, glossy discs, warm disco-pop lights and a neon title. Poker chips splash across the screen at the start of every game and rain down when someone wins.

[`design.md`](design.md) holds every tunable value: the wooden background, option boxes, buttons and icon buttons, scoreboard, board frame and border, bulbs, felt and squares, discs, disc flip/drop animations, hints, dialogs, the poker chips and the roulette wheel. Edit a value, save, and the running app reloads with it. The build checks that tokens and code agree (a missing token fails the build, an unused one warns). The redesign is committed as e1a4621, and Cafe mode is gone. I checked the result in screenshots of the UI, not by playing a game in the app window. The Rust tests (40) pass, clippy is clean, and the UI type-checks and builds.

What changed - Wooden background: the mahogany texture from wooden_bg.png fills the page, with a warm lamp glow, slow coloured light washes and a golden glint sweeping across the grain. The same wood is used on the board frame and the option boxes. - Brass: every button has a brass rim with a slow sheen, and the main button is solid polished brass. The frame, option boxes, scoreboard and inputs are brass-trimmed. - Red velvet: button faces use the velvet texture. The game controls (Home, Undo, Hint, Resign, New game) are now round velvet icon buttons with brass glyphs and labels. - Green felt: I used green-velvet.png as the board's playing surface, with thin grid lines. You didn't say where it should go. It also makes the black and white discs stand out more than wood squares would. - Roulette wheel: inspo2.png inspired a slow-turning red and black wheel behind the spinning coin on the home screen. - Chip splash at game start: about 34 chips fly in from the bottom and sides, arc across the screen, tumble, land, bounce and fade over roughly 3 seconds. You can keep playing while it runs. - Chip rain on a win: about 60 chips fall from the top while the result dialog is open. Chips rain on a win but not when you lose to the computer. Both animations are skipped when Settings > Animations is off.

design.md is rebuilt around these materials, so you can change the wood tint, brass colour, felt, chip count, colours and timings. I removed the ui_mode setting along with Cafe. Settings files that still contain it load fine.

Check before sharing - Textures: I copied the wood and both velvet textures from Design-inspo/ into ui/public/textures/ so the app can ship them. I don't know their licence, so check it before a public release. - Inspiration photos: I git-ignored the Design-inspo/ folder itself, because the photos are large and probably not mine to publish. - Chip numbers: while chips tumble, their printed values look mirrored for a moment. That's just the 3D flip. - Splash and rain: I checked both animations by freezing them partway through in headless Firefox, not by watching them run live.

Turn 118

instead of having one vignette, have only wood, have a border lighting - red green blue, moving pattern and only the glow effect from that
Claude's response

I'm doing three things: 1. Wood only: the dark vignette, the lamp glow, the drifting coloured washes and the golden glint all go. The background is the wood texture with just a light darkening so the text stays readable. 2. Border lighting: a red, green and blue light runs around the window edge as a conic sweep, so the colours chase each other around the border. 3. Glow only: the light is a thin ring blurred heavily, so you see it as a coloured glow bleeding in from the edges, with no hard bar. A second wider, fainter layer adds reach.

The blur has to sit on a wrapper above the mask, since CSS applies masks after filters, so a blur on the masked ring would leave a hard edge.

The background is now plain wood lit only by an animated red-green-blue border glow, committed as 348571a. I checked it in screenshots of the home and game screens, with the light caught at several points around the border. I haven't watched the animation run live in the app window. The Rust tests pass, and the UI type-checks and builds without warnings.

What changed - Wood only: the dark vignette, warm lamp glow, drifting coloured washes and golden sweep are gone. What's left is the wood texture with a light darkening (main_bg_tint) so text stays readable. Set it to 0 for completely untouched wood. - Border lighting: a red, green and blue light runs round the window edge. You see only its glow, a coloured haze bleeding in from the edges with no hard bar, plus a wider, fainter halo behind it. It sweeps continuously round the window once every 7 seconds. - Settings: the light respects Settings > Animations. With animations off, the glow stays still at a fixed spot instead of disappearing.

Tuning: design.md has a new "Border lighting" section with these values: - border_light_red, border_light_green and border_light_blue set the three colours. - border_light_pattern sets the colour stops. Repeat the three colours for two sweeps round the border. - border_light_width and border_light_glow set the glow's strength and how far it reaches in. - border_light_halo and border_light_halo_opacity set the wider haze. - border_light_spin_duration sets the speed. - border_light_opacity sets the overall strength.

My first version was too faint, because blurring a thin ring spreads it very thin. I thickened it, and the committed defaults are the stronger ones.

Not changed: the yellow marquee bulbs on the board frame and the pulsing hint rings are separate effects and still there. If you want the board frame calmer too, say so and I'll tone them down.

The window-fitting layout and the new LED-strip border light are committed as 33d3fa1. I checked them in screenshots at several window sizes, but I haven't run the app in its real window.

The Rust tests pass, the UI type-checks and builds, and I removed my temporary test files.

Layout fits the window

  • Game screen: the board is sized from both the width and the height left over, so it's never cut off or oversized. It sits in a grid with the title bar, scoreboard, status line, controls and move list.
  • Wide windows: the board fills the height on the left, and the scoreboard (stacked), controls and move list form a column on the right.
  • Narrow or tall windows: everything stacks in one column.
  • Smaller windows: the board frame and its bulbs shrink with the board. In very short windows the move list is dropped to give the board room.
  • Messages: the pass banner and errors are now floating notices, so they no longer push the board around.
  • Other screens: the home screen scales its wheel, title and buttons to the window height. Setup, Settings and the result dialog fit too.
  • Tested sizes: 480×600 (your minimum), 700×1000 and 1200×720. At 480×600 the home, game, settings and result screens all show everything.

LED strip lighting

I used lighting strip.png, the multicoloured addressable strip you added. The border light is now a real strip of little LEDs round all four window edges: - Each bulb has its own colour (red, pink, purple, blue, cyan, green, yellow) and its own glow. - The colour pattern flows clockwise round the window. - The bulbs twinkle in two interleaved sets, like the marquee bulbs on the board frame. - Content keeps clear of the strip.

design.md has a rewritten "Border lighting" section where you can tune: - the colour pattern, bulb size, spacing, glow, and distance from the edge - the flow speed and the twinkle speed and dimness

Known gaps: - A couple of bulbs at the board frame's corners overlap slightly. - I only caught the strip in still frames, so the flowing motion and twinkle are untested live. - Window sizes below 480×600 would scroll.

Claude's response

This is a substantial piece of work, so I'm laying out the approach first.

The desktop game's engine is in Rust behind Tauri, and a static page on GitHub Pages can't run that. For the web version I'll port the engine to TypeScript and prove it against the same golden file used for the Rust engine (perft counts and 100 recorded games, including forced passes). Then the web page is the same Svelte UI, with the same styling, textures, LED strip and chip animations, running on a browser backend instead of Tauri.

The output is a single self-contained HTML file, with the JS, CSS, fonts and textures all inlined. You can drop it anywhere and link to it, and it works offline too.

I'll start with the engine port.

// 8x8 Othello on BigInt bitboards: a TypeScript port of the Rust `othello-core` Position, used by the
// web build (the desktop app uses the Rust engine). Same conventions: square (row, col) is bit
// row*8+col, a1 = 0 (top-left), h8 = 63, pass = 64, Black moves first. It is checked against the same
// golden file as the Rust engine (see engine.test.ts).
//
// Written in "erasable" TypeScript (no enums or parameter properties) so Node can run it directly.

export type Side = 'black' | 'white';
export type Outcome = 'black' | 'white' | 'draw';

export const SIZE = 8;
export const NUM_SQUARES = 64;
export const PASS = 64;
export const FULL = (1n << 64n) - 1n;

const COL_A = 0x0101010101010101n;
const COL_H = COL_A << 7n;

/** [shift left?, shift amount, mask of squares a shifted bit may land on] */
const DIRS: [boolean, bigint, bigint][] = [
  [false, 9n, FULL ^ COL_H], // up-left
  [false, 8n, FULL], // up
  [false, 7n, FULL ^ COL_A], // up-right
  [false, 1n, FULL ^ COL_H], // left
  [true, 1n, FULL ^ COL_A], // right
  [true, 7n, FULL ^ COL_H], // down-left
  [true, 8n, FULL], // down
  [true, 9n, FULL ^ COL_A] // down-right
];

const shift = (x: bigint, left: boolean, n: bigint, mask: bigint): bigint =>
  (left ? x << n : x >> n) & mask;

export const popcount = (x: bigint): number => {
  let n = 0;
  while (x) {
    x &= x - 1n;
    n++;
  }
  return n;
};

export const opponent = (s: Side): Side => (s === 'black' ? 'white' : 'black');

/** Why a move was refused. */
export class IllegalMoveError extends Error {
  readonly reason: 'game_over' | 'not_legal' | 'pass_not_allowed';
  constructor(reason: 'game_over' | 'not_legal' | 'pass_not_allowed', message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.reason = reason;
  }
}

export interface Played {
  position: Position;
  /** Bitboard of the discs this move flipped (0n for a pass). */
  flipped: bigint;
}

/** An immutable position. Cheap to copy, so search and history can keep copies freely. */
export class Position {
  readonly black: bigint;
  readonly white: bigint;
  readonly toMove: Side;
  /** Consecutive passes so far; 2 ends the game. */
  readonly passes: number;

  constructor(black: bigint, white: bigint, toMove: Side, passes = 0) {
    if (black & white) throw new Error('black and white discs overlap');
    if (passes < 0 || passes > 2) throw new Error('passes must be 0..2');
    this.black = black;
    this.white = white;
    this.toMove = toMove;
    this.passes = passes;
  }

  /** Standard start: white on d4/e5, black on e4/d5, Black to move. */
  static initial(): Position {
    const bit = (r: number, c: number) => 1n << BigInt(r * SIZE + c);
    return new Position(bit(3, 4) | bit(4, 3), bit(3, 3) | bit(4, 4), 'black', 0);
  }

  get own(): bigint {
    return this.toMove === 'black' ? this.black : this.white;
  }

  get opp(): bigint {
    return this.toMove === 'black' ? this.white : this.black;
  }

  counts(): { black: number; white: number } {
    return { black: popcount(this.black), white: popcount(this.white) };
  }

  /** Two consecutive passes, or a full board. */
  isTerminal(): boolean {
    return this.passes >= 2 || (this.black | this.white) === FULL;
  }

  /** Bitboard of squares where the side to move can place a disc. */
  legalBits(): bigint {
    const own = this.own;
    const opp = this.opp;
    const empty = FULL ^ (own | opp);
    let moves = 0n;
    for (const [left, n, mask] of DIRS) {
      let x = shift(own, left, n, mask) & opp;
      for (let i = 0; i < SIZE - 3; i++) x |= shift(x, left, n, mask) & opp;
      moves |= shift(x, left, n, mask) & empty;
    }
    return moves;
  }

  /** Legal moves in ascending square order: [PASS] if there is no placement, [] once the game is over. */
  legalMoves(): number[] {
    if (this.isTerminal()) return [];
    let bits = this.legalBits();
    if (bits === 0n) return [PASS];
    const moves: number[] = [];
    for (let sq = 0; bits; sq++, bits >>= 1n) if (bits & 1n) moves.push(sq);
    ret

import { Position, PASS, moveName, parseMove, type Outcome, type Side } from './position.ts';

const golden = JSON.parse(
  readFileSync(new URL('../../../../tests/golden/engine_8x8.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')
);

interface State { black: string; white: string; player: Side; passes: number }
const position = (s: State) => new Position(BigInt('0x' + s.black), BigInt('0x' + s.white), s.player, s.passes);
const perft = (p: Position, depth: number): number =>
  depth === 0 || p.isTerminal() ? 1 : p.legalMoves().reduce((n, m) => n + perft(p.play(m).position, depth - 1), 0);

test('start position matches the reference', () => {
  const start = position(golden.meta.encoding.start_position);
  const p = Position.initial();
  assert.equal(p.black, start.black);
  assert.equal(p.white, start.white);
  assert.equal(p.toMove, 'black');
});

test('perft matches the reference (depth 1-7)', () => {
  for (const [depth, expected] of Object.entries(golden.perft)) {
    assert.equal(perft(Position.initial(), Number(depth)), expected, `perft depth ${depth}`);
  }
});

function replay(game: any) {
  const name: string = game.name;
  let pos = position(game.start);
  game.plies.forEach((ply: any, i: number) => {
    const where = `${name} ply ${i}`;
    const expected = position(ply.state);
    assert.ok(pos.black === expected.black && pos.white === expected.white && pos.toMove === expected.toMove && pos.passes === expected.passes, `${where}: position drifted`);
    assert.deepEqual(pos.legalMoves(), ply.legal, `${where}: legal moves`);
    pos = pos.play(ply.move).position;
    const after = position(ply.after);
    assert.ok(pos.black === after.black && pos.white === after.white && pos.toMove === after.toMove && pos.passes === after.passes, `${where}: position after ${moveName(ply.move)}`);
  });
  const fin = game.final;
  const end = position(fin.state);
  assert.ok(pos.black === end.black && pos.white === end.white && pos.passes === end.passes, `${name}: final position`);
  assert.equal(pos.isTerminal(), fin.terminal, `${name}: terminal`);
  assert.deepEqual(pos.legalMoves(), fin.legal, `${name}: final legal moves`);
  if (pos.isTerminal()) {
    const { black, white } = pos.counts();
    assert.equal(black, fin.black_discs, `${name}: black discs`);
    assert.equal(white, fin.white_discs, `${name}: white discs`);
    assert.equal(pos.outcome() as Outcome, fin.winner, `${name}: outcome`);
  }
}

test('hand-built rule cases match the reference', () => {
  assert.ok(golden.cases.length > 0);
  golden.cases.forEach(replay);
});

test('100 seeded random games match the reference', () => {
  assert.ok(golden.games.length > 0);
  golden.games.forEach(replay);
});

test('illegal moves are refused', () => {
  const p = Position.initial();
  assert.throws(() => p.play(0), /not a legal move|flips nothing/);
  assert.throws(() => p.play(27), /occupied/);
  assert.throws(() => p.play(PASS), /cannot pass/);
  assert.throws(() => p.play(99), /not a legal move/);
});

test('move names round-trip', () => {
  for (let i = 0; i <= 64; i++) assert.equal(parseMove(moveName(i)), i);
  assert.equal(parseMove('i1'), null);
  assert.equal(moveName(19), 'd3');
});

// Computer opponents for the web build (the desktop app will use Oroletto; this build has no
// neural network, so its four levels are classic bots):
//   1 random · 2 greedy (most discs next move) · 3 alpha-beta depth 3 · 4 alpha-beta, iterative
//   deepening within a time budget. Levels 3 and 4 use the heuristic from OthelloRL's tuned bot
//   (corners 50, mobility 5, discs 1, X-squares -25).
//
// The search runs on a plain 64-cell array (faster than BigInt bitboards), in slices that yield to the
// browser between depths so the page keeps animating while the computer thinks.

import { PASS, Position, type Side } from './position.ts';

/** Small seedable generator (splitmix64), so games can be reproduced in tests. */
export class Rng {
  private state: bigint;
  constructor(seed: number | bigint) {
    this.state = BigInt(seed) & ((1n << 64n) - 1n);
  }
  nextU64(): bigint {
    const M = (1n << 64n) - 1n;
    this.state = (this.state + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15n) & M;
    let z = this.state;
    z = ((z ^ (z >> 30n)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9n) & M;
    z = ((z ^ (z >> 27n)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebn) & M;
    return z ^ (z >> 31n);
  }
  /** Uniform integer in 0..n-1. */
  below(n: number): number {
    return Number((this.nextU64() * BigInt(n)) >> 64n);
  }
  pick<T>(items: readonly T[]): T {
    return items[this.below(items.length)];
  }
}

export interface SearchControl {
  /** True once the game was undone, restarted or resigned: stop and return null. */
  cancelled(): boolean;
  /** 0..1, drives the "thinking" indicator. */
  progress(fraction: number): void;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ mailbox board

type Board = Int8Array; // 0 empty, 1 black, 2 white
const DR = [-1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1];
const DC = [-1, 0, 1, -1, 1, -1, 0, 1];
const CORNERS = [0, 7, 56, 63];
// X-squares (diagonal to a corner) paired with their corner.
const X_SQUARES: [number, number][] = [[9, 0], [14, 7], [49, 56], [54, 63]];

const code = (s: Side) => (s === 'black' ? 1 : 2);

function toBoard(p: Position): Board {
  const b = new Int8Array(64);
  for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
    const bit = 1n << BigInt(i);
    b[i] = p.black & bit ? 1 : p.white & bit ? 2 : 0;
  }
  return b;
}

/** Squares flipped if `me` plays `sq` (empty list: not legal). */
function flipsAt(b: Board, sq: number, me: number): number[] {
  if (b[sq] !== 0) return [];
  const them = 3 - me;
  const r0 = sq >> 3;
  const c0 = sq & 7;
  const flips: number[] = [];
  for (let d = 0; d < 8; d++) {
    let r = r0 + DR[d];
    let c = c0 + DC[d];
    const line: number[] = [];
    while (r >= 0 && r < 8 && c >= 0 && c < 8 && b[r * 8 + c] === them) {
      line.push(r * 8 + c);
      r += DR[d];
      c += DC[d];
    }
    if (line.length && r >= 0 && r < 8 && c >= 0 && c < 8 && b[r * 8 + c] === me) flips.push(...line);
  }
  return flips;
}

function movesOf(b: Board, me: number): number[] {
  const out: number[] = [];
  for (let sq = 0; sq < 64; sq++) if (b[sq] === 0 && flipsAt(b, sq, me).length) out.push(sq);
  return out;
}

function mobilityOf(b: Board, me: number): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (let sq = 0; sq < 64; sq++) if (b[sq] === 0 && flipsAt(b, sq, me).length) n++;
  return n;
}

function play(b: Board, sq: number, me: number, flips: number[]): Board {
  const nb = b.slice();
  nb[sq] = me;
  for (const f of flips) nb[f] = me;
  return nb;
}

const discDiff = (b: Board, me: number): number => {
  let d = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) d += b[i] === me ? 1 : b[i] === 0 ? 0 : -1;
  return d;
};

/** Heuristic value of a position for `me`. */
function evaluate(b: Board, me: number): number {
  const them = 3 - me;
  let corners = 0;
  for (const c of CORNERS) corners += b[c] === me ? 1 : b[c] === them ? -1 : 0;
  let xsq = 0;
  for (const [x, c] of X_SQUARES) if (b[c] === 0) xsq += b[x] === me ? 1 : b[x] === them ? -1 : 0;
  return discDiff(b, me) + 5 * (mobilityOf(b, me) - mobilityOf(b, them)) + 50 * corners - 25 * xsq;
}

 * Best root moves (every move tied for the top score) at a fixed depth. Later moves are searched
 * with a window just below the current best, so ties stay exact while worse moves are pruned.
 */
function searchRoot(b: Board, me: number, depth: number, clock: { nodes: number; deadline: number }): { best: number[]; score: number } {
  let best: number[] = [];
  let top = -Infinity;
  for (const m of order(movesOf(b, me))) {
    const alphaRoot = top === -Infinity ? -Infinity : top - 1;
    const v = -negamax(play(b, m, me, flipsAt(b, m, me)), 3 - me, depth - 1, -Infinity, -alphaRoot, false, clock);
    if (v > top) {
      top = v;
      best = [m];
    } else if (v === top) best.push(m);
  }
  return { best, score: top };
}

// The game session for the web build: a TypeScript port of the Rust `othello-api` Session, so the same
// UI runs unchanged in the browser. Same rules of the road:
//  - forced passes are played automatically and announced with a `passed` event;
//  - every change of game bumps a generation counter, so a computer move that finishes after an
//    undo, new game or resignation is discarded;
//  - undo rolls back to just before your latest placement (vs the computer: the latest one made on
//    your turn), taking automatic passes with it.

import type { ApiError, Awaiting, GameEvent, Mode, Side as ApiSide, Snapshot, Status } from '../api.ts';
import { Rng, chooseMove, type SearchControl } from './ai.ts';
import { PASS, Position, bitsToSquares, moveName, opponent, type Side } from './position.ts';

interface Entry {
  position: Position;
  /** The move that led here and the discs it flipped; null for the start. */
  last: { move: number; flipped: bigint } | null;
}

interface Active {
  history: Entry[];
  /** Resolved: `human` is never 'random'. */
  mode: Mode;
  human: Side | null;
  resigned: Side | null;
}

export interface SessionOptions {
  seed?: number;
  /** The computer waits at least this long before moving, so you see your own move first. */
  minThinkMs?: number;
  /** Time budget of the strongest level. */
  level4BudgetMs?: number;
}

const fail = (error: ApiError): never => {
  throw error;
};
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

export class WebSession {
  private active: Active | null = null;
  private generation = 0;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<(event: GameEvent) => void>();
  private readonly rng: Rng;
  private readonly minThinkMs: number;
  private readonly level4BudgetMs: number;
  private ticker: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;

  constructor(options: SessionOptions = {}) {
    this.rng = new Rng(options.seed ?? Date.now());
    this.minThinkMs = options.minThinkMs ?? 650;
    this.level4BudgetMs = options.level4BudgetMs ?? 900;
  }

  /** Subscribe to events. Returns the function that unsubscribes. */
  onEvent(handler: (event: GameEvent) => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(handler);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(handler);
  }

  private emit(events: GameEvent[]) {
    for (const e of events) this.listeners.forEach((h) => h(e));
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ commands

  newGame(mode: Mode, position: Position = Position.initial()): Snapshot {
    if (mode.kind === 'vs_computer' && !(Number.isInteger(mode.difficulty) && mode.difficulty >= 1 && mode.difficulty <= 4)) {
      fail({ code: 'invalid_difficulty', given: mode.difficulty });
    }
    this.cancelSearch();
    let resolved: Mode = mode;
    let human: Side | null = null;
    if (mode.kind === 'vs_computer') {
      human = mode.human === 'random' ? (this.rng.below(2) === 0 ? 'black' : 'white') : mode.human;
      resolved = { kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty: mode.difficulty, human };
    }
    this.active = { history: [{ position, last: null }], mode: resolved, human, resigned: null };
    const events = this.advance();
    const snapshot = this.buildSnapshot();
    this.emit(events);
    return snapshot;
  }

// Drives the web session the way the UI does: commands in, snapshots and events out.
// Run with:  npm test

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import type { GameEvent, Mode, Snapshot } from '../api.ts';
import { Rng, chooseMove, greedyBest } from './ai.ts';
import { PASS, Position, parseMove, type Side } from './position.ts';
import { WebSession } from './session.ts';

const sq = (name: string) => parseMove(name)!;
const twoPlayers: Mode = { kind: 'two_players' };
const vs = (human: 'black' | 'white' | 'random', difficulty: number): Mode => ({ kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty, human });

function make(opts: ConstructorParameters<typeof WebSession>[0] = {}) {
  const session = new WebSession({ seed: 1, minThinkMs: 5, level4BudgetMs: 40, ...opts });
  const events: GameEvent[] = [];
  session.onEvent((e) => events.push(e));
  /** Wait until a state_changed satisfying `pred` has arrived (or time out). */
  const waitState = async (pred: (s: Snapshot) => boolean, ms = 4000): Promise<Snapshot> => {
    const end = Date.now() + ms;
    for (;;) {
      const hit = events.find((e) => e.type === 'state_changed' && pred(e.snapshot));
      if (hit && hit.type === 'state_changed') return hit.snapshot;
      if (Date.now() > end) throw new Error('timed out waiting for a state');
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5));
    }
  };
  return { session, events, waitState };
}

const rejects = (fn: () => unknown, code: string) =>
  assert.throws(fn, (e: any) => e && e.code === code, `expected ${code}`);

// The browser backend: the same commands the Tauri shell exposes, served by the TypeScript engine,
// with settings kept in localStorage. Used when the page runs outside the desktop app.

import type { GameEvent, Mode, Settings, Snapshot } from '../api.ts';
import { WebSession } from './session.ts';

const SETTINGS_KEY = 'othello-player.settings';

export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: Settings = {
  show_legal_moves: true,
  animations: true,
  sound: true,
  default_difficulty: 2,
  default_human_side: 'black'
};

/** Read saved settings; anything missing or malformed falls back to the default. */
export function loadSettings(): Settings {
  try {
    const raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(SETTINGS_KEY) ?? '{}');
    const s = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };
    if (typeof raw.show_legal_moves === 'boolean') s.show_legal_moves = raw.show_legal_moves;
    if (typeof raw.animations === 'boolean') s.animations = raw.animations;
    if (typeof raw.sound === 'boolean') s.sound = raw.sound;
    if (Number.isInteger(raw.default_difficulty) && raw.default_difficulty >= 1 && raw.default_difficulty <= 4) {
      s.default_difficulty = raw.default_difficulty;
    }
    if (['black', 'white', 'random'].includes(raw.default_human_side)) s.default_human_side = raw.default_human_side;
    return s;
  } catch {
    return { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };
  }
}

export function createWebBackend() {
  const session = new WebSession();
  return {
    newGame: async (mode: Mode): Promise<Snapshot> => session.newGame(mode),
    play: async (square: number): Promise<Snapshot> => session.play(square),
    undo: async (): Promise<Snapshot> => session.undo(),
    resign: async (): Promise<Snapshot> => session.resign(),
    snapshot: async (): Promise<Snapshot> => session.snapshot(),
    hint: (): Promise<number> => session.hint(),
    getSettings: async (): Promise<Settings> => loadSettings(),
    setSettings: async (settings: Settings): Promise<void> => {
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(SETTINGS_KEY, JSON.stringify(settings));
      } catch {
        /* private mode or storage blocked: settings just won't persist */
      }
    },
    onEvent: (handler: (event: GameEvent) => void): (() => void) => session.onEvent(handler)
  };
}

open("single-file-plugin.ts","w").write('''// For the web build: folds the bundled JS and CSS into index.html so the whole game is one
// self-contained .html file (fonts and textures are already inlined as data: URIs).
import type { Plugin } from 'vite';

const key = (url: string) => url.replace(/^(\\.\\/|\\/)/, '');

export default function singleFile(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: 'othello-single-file',
    enforce: 'post',
    transformIndexHtml: {
      order: 'post',
      handler(html, ctx) {
        const bundle = ctx.bundle;
        if (!bundle) return html;
        return html
          .replace(/<script\\b[^>]*\\bsrc="([^"]+)"[^>]*><\\/script>/g, (tag, src: string) => {
            const file = bundle[key(src)];
            if (!file || file.type !== 'chunk') return tag;
            delete bundle[key(src)];
            // "</script" inside the code would end the tag early.
            return `<script type="module">${file.code.replace(/<\\/script/gi, '<\\\\/script')}</script>`;
          })
          .replace(/<link\\b[^>]*rel="stylesheet"[^>]*href="([^"]+)"[^>]*>/g, (tag, href: string) => {
            const file = bundle[key(href)];
            if (!file || file.type !== 'asset') return tag;
            delete bundle[key(href)];
            return `<style>${String(file.source)}</style>`;
          });
      }
    }
  };
}
''')

function inlineTextures(css: string): string {
  const defs = new Map<string, string>();
  const body = css.replace(/url\\((['"]?)\\/(textures\\/[^)'"]+)\\1\\)/g, (_m, _q, rel: string) => {

    return `var(${name})`;

}

[`web/othello.html`](web/othello.html) is the whole game as **one self-contained file** (about 260 KB: the code, fonts and textures are all inside it). It looks and plays like the desktop app: same wood, brass, velvet, LED strip and chip animations. It needs no server and no network, and it even works opened straight from disk.

**To put it on your GitHub Pages site**, copy the file into your site's repository and link to it:

```
your-site/othello/index.html     <- a copy of web/othello.html
```
```html
<a href="/othello/">Play Othello</a>
<!-- or embed it in a page -->
<iframe src="/othello/" title="Othello" style="width:100%;height:90vh;border:0"></iframe>
```
(If you copy it as `othello.html` instead, link to `/othello.html`.)

Differences from the desktop app:
- The computer is a classic bot, not Oroletto (the neural network is not in the browser build). The four levels are **1 Easy** random, **2 Medium** greedy (most discs next move), **3 Hard** alpha-beta search 3 moves deep, **4 Master** alpha-beta with iterative deepening for about 0.9 s per move.
- Settings are kept in the browser (localStorage).

Rebuild it after changing the UI or `design.md` (this regenerates `web/othello.html`):

```bash
cd ui && npm install     # once
npm run build:web
```

The page runs on a TypeScript port of the Rust engine (`ui/src/lib/engine/`). `npm test` checks that port against the same golden file as the Rust engine (perft, hand-built rule cases and 100 recorded games), plus the session logic and the bots; `npm run test:web` drives the built page end to end in a headless DOM (start a game, play, undo, play a whole game, change a setting).

The web page is built and committed as 31fe324, and your link target is web/othello.html. It's one self-contained 260 KB file with the code, fonts and textures inside, so it needs no server and no network. It even works opened straight from disk.

To put it on your site: copy it into your Pages repository (for example as othello/index.html) and link to it with <a href="/othello/">Play Othello</a>. You can also embed it with <iframe src="/othello/" style="width:100%;height:90vh;border:0">. The README has both snippets.

How well it matches the app: it's the same UI, not a lookalike. I opened the built file in Firefox, and the home screen is indistinguishable from the desktop app. The game screen also works there, with the wood, LED strip, velvet and brass buttons, felt board, and the wide two-column layout. I didn't see the chip splash or chip rain in the browser, only the splash mounting in the DOM test. The Light/Dark theme isn't a factor, because the casino look is the only look.

How it works: the desktop game's engine is Rust, which can't run on a static page. So I ported the engine and session logic to TypeScript, and the UI picks Tauri or the browser engine automatically.

What I checked - Rules engine: the port matches the same reference data the Rust engine uses: perft to depth 7, the six rule cases, and all 100 recorded games including forced passes. - Session and bots: 27 TypeScript tests (npm test) cover the session behaviour and the bots. The stronger bots beat random and greedy opponents clearly. - Whole page, headless: a DOM test (npm run test:web) loads the built file and clicks through it. It starts a game, makes a move, and watches the computer reply on its own. It then undoes, plays a full game to the result dialog, changes a setting and confirms it's saved, and finds no script errors. - Desktop app: the Rust tests, clippy and the desktop build still pass.

Differences from the desktop app - Opponent: the browser has no neural network, so Oroletto isn't there. The four levels are classic bots: 1. Easy: random 2. Medium: greedy (most discs next move) 3. Hard: alpha-beta search, 3 moves deep 4. Master: alpha-beta search for about 0.9 s per move - Settings: they're stored in the browser, so they won't carry between devices. - Desktop levels: the desktop's top three levels still use the placeholder greedy bot until Oroletto is wired in. - Computer pause: the computer waits about 0.65 s before moving, so you see your own move first.

Keeping it current: web/othello.html is generated. After changing the UI or design.md, rebuild it with cd ui && npm run build:web.

Textures: I converted the three textures from PNG to JPEG, which shrank them from about 680 KB to about 56 KB. As before, their licence is unknown, so check it before publishing the page.

I have a website public using github pages. I want to be able to link this game there. So that if anyone clicks on play they can play the game for free insie the website itself. how to do that?
Claude's response

The game is one self-contained file, so putting it on your site takes three steps. I haven't tried these steps on your actual site, so say if anything behaves differently.

1. Add the game file to your site

  1. Open your GitHub Pages repository, the one that serves your public site.
  2. Create a folder for the game, for example othello/.
  3. Copy web/othello.html from this repo into it and name it index.html, so you have othello/index.html.
  4. Commit and push. After a minute or so, the game is live at https://<your-site>/othello/.

That alone gives you a link anyone can click to play, hosted on your own domain.

2. Play inside a page of your site (click-to-play)

To have a "Play" button that opens the game inside your own page, paste this into the page where you want it. The game loads only when someone clicks, so the page stays fast:

<div style="max-width:760px;margin:2rem auto;text-align:center">
  <button id="othello-play"
    style="font:700 1.2rem Georgia,serif;padding:.9rem 2.2rem;border-radius:999px;
           border:3px solid #c9a24e;background:#a3182a;color:#fff4e0;cursor:pointer">
    Play Othello, free
  </button>
</div>
<script>
  document.getElementById('othello-play').addEventListener('click', function () {
    var f = document.createElement('iframe');
    f.src = 'othello/index.html';       // path to the game, relative to this page
    f.title = 'Othello';
    f.allowFullscreen = true;
    f.style.cssText = 'width:100%;height:min(88vh,820px);border:0;border-radius:16px;' +
                      'box-shadow:0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.4)';
    this.parentNode.replaceChild(f, this);   // swap the button for the game
  });
</script>

If you'd rather have it visible straight away, skip the button and paste <iframe src="othello/index.html" title="Othello" allowfullscreen style="width:100%;height:88vh;border:0"></iframe>.

Things to watch

  • Link paths: if your site lives at username.github.io/some-repo/ and not at the root, use a relative path like othello/index.html. An absolute /othello/ would point at the wrong place.
  • Size: the game resizes to fit its frame, down to about 480×600. Give it at least that much room; a tall frame on a phone works well.
  • Jekyll: if your site uses Jekyll, a plain HTML file in a normal folder is served as-is. Avoid folder names starting with _.
  • Sandboxing: if you add a sandbox attribute to the iframe, include allow-scripts allow-same-origin, otherwise the game can't run or save its settings.

Updating later

When I change the game, web/othello.html is regenerated here, and you copy the new file over othello/index.html and push. If you'd like it to update itself, I can make this repo publish the page through GitHub Pages and your site would just point at that address. That needs the file moved into a docs/ folder. Tell me if you want that.

# Putting the game on your GitHub Pages site

Two files do everything:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `web/othello.html` | the whole game (one self-contained page, no other files needed) |
| `web/embed/play-button.html` | a "Play Othello" button that opens the game inside your page |

## Steps

1. **Upload the game.** In your site's repository, make a folder (say `othello/`) and put a copy of
   `web/othello.html` in it, named `index.html` → `othello/index.html`.
2. **Add the button.** Open the page of your site where the Play button should appear and paste the
   contents of `web/embed/play-button.html` where you want it. If that page is not in the same folder
   as `othello/`, change `data-src` in the button to the path from that page to the game.
3. **Publish.** Commit and push your site's repository. GitHub Pages updates in about a minute.
4. **Try it.** Hard-refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R), click the button, and play a move.

## If something is off

- **"404" or a blank frame:** `data-src` is wrong. It is relative to the page holding the button.
  For a project site at `username.github.io/repo/` do not start the path with `/`.
- **You still see the old game after an update:** hard-refresh; browsers cache the file.
- **You added `sandbox` to the iframe:** it needs `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` or the game cannot run.

## Updating the game later

Rebuild with `cd ui && npm run build:web` (this rewrites `web/othello.html`), copy the new file over
`othello/index.html` in your site, and push.

Turn 123

how will it work?
Claude's response

It works in four stages.

1. Your site holds two things. - Your page, with a "Play Othello, free" button. - The game, which is one self-contained file at othello/index.html. The engine, bots, graphics, fonts and textures are all inside it, about 260 KB.

2. A visitor opens your page. Only the button loads. The game isn't fetched yet, so your page stays fast.

3. The visitor clicks the button. A small script replaces the button with an <iframe>, a window inside your page, pointing at othello/index.html. The browser downloads the game file from your GitHub Pages site and runs it in that frame.

4. The visitor plays. Everything runs in their browser, with no server, no account and no cost to you or them. - The rules, the computer opponents and the undo all run as JavaScript on their machine. - Their settings, such as animations and default difficulty, are saved in their own browser storage. They aren't shared between visitors. - GitHub Pages only serves static files. It never runs any game code, which is why this works on free hosting.

What visitors get. The web version's four levels are classic bots: random, greedy, and two lookahead searches. It doesn't use the Oroletto model. I added no model to the web build, and its logic is the TypeScript port described above. The desktop app is where Oroletto will go.

Limits. - Two players on one device works. Playing against a friend on another device doesn't, because that needs a server. - The game file is a copy. If you change the game here, rebuild with cd ui && npm run build:web and copy web/othello.html over othello/index.html in your site repo again.
