### 3.3 Play vs Computer — difficulty levels
**Four levels, one model, one knob.** Every level is played by the same network, **the strongest 8×8 Oroletto model**, with the **same MCTS search budget**. Levels differ **only in the move temperature T**:
- After searching, the move is sampled from the root visit counts with probability ∝ N^(1/T).
- **T = 0** plays the most-visited move (full strength). **Higher T** spreads probability over the other moves the search visited, so play becomes more varied and makes more mistakes.
- There is **no root noise** and no change in the number of simulations between levels.

| Level | Name | Simulations | Temperature T |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Easy | shared (≈200) | high (placeholder 2.0) |
| 2 | Medium | shared | placeholder 1.0 |
| 3 | Hard | shared | placeholder 0.25 |
| 4 | Master | shared | 0 (most-visited move) |

The values are **placeholders** until OthelloRL calibrates them on the 8×8 model (OthelloRL PLAN Step 5.7):
- the shared simulation count is the largest that keeps the worst-case move within the 2 s budget;
- the four temperatures are chosen from candidates {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4} so that each level beats the one below it at least 70% of the time.

The calibrated values are delivered in the model manifest (`models/oroletto-8x8.json`, fields `levels.sims` and `levels.ladder[].temperature`). They are read at runtime, not hard-coded.

- The AI must respond within **≤ 2 s per move** on a typical laptop at every level. Every level uses the same search, so they all cost the same.
- The rule-based bots from OthelloRL (random, greedy, heuristic, minimax) are **not** player levels. They are kept as test baselines and as stand-ins during development before the model is ready.
- Temperature applies only to the in-game move choice. Hints and the parity test use temperature 0.

Turn 125

why does it say that T=0 plays the mo0st visited move? it should play the best predicted move right without any guess work ?
Claude's response

"Most-visited" is the search's best move, and it is deterministic. There's no guessing at T=0.

Why visits rather than a score - The network gives a policy (how promising each move looks) and a value (who is winning). - MCTS then runs 200 simulations. Each one walks down the tree, picking the move with the best mix of its average value so far and the network's prior (PUCT). Promising moves get more simulations. - After 200 simulations, the visit counts are the search's verdict. A move gets visited a lot only if it kept looking best as the search learned more.

Why not pick the highest average value or the raw policy - Highest average value: a move visited only 2 times can show a lucky high average. Visit count is robust to that, because a move can't accumulate many visits unless it held up under scrutiny. - Raw policy argmax: that is the network's first impression with no lookahead. Search corrects its mistakes, so it plays weaker than the search result. - This is the standard AlphaZero rule. The visit counts are also what the network was trained to imitate.

What T does - The move is chosen with probability proportional to N^(1/T). As T goes to 0, all the probability goes to the highest N, which is the argmax. So T=0 means no randomness. - The only randomness left at T=0 is a tie, when two moves have exactly the same visit count. Then one is picked at random. Both are equally good by the search's own measure.

Where it's pinned down - The spec says Master (T=0) plays the most-visited move. The parity test requires the app to reproduce OthelloRL's exact visit counts. So Master's choices are fully determined by the search.

Turn 126

I want to know how you are using one model for 4 different levels
Claude's response

One network plays all four levels. Each level changes only how the final move is chosen from the search results.

What every level does 1. Run MCTS with the Oroletto network for 200 simulations. The search is identical at all four levels. 2. That gives a visit count N for each legal move. For example, one position might give: d3 = 120, c4 = 50, f5 = 20, e6 = 10. 3. Pick the move with probability proportional to N^(1/T). Only T changes between levels.

The same position at each level

Level T How the choice behaves
4 Master 0 Always d3, the most-visited move.
3 Hard 1.0 Probability follows the visit shares: d3 about 60%, c4 25%, f5 10%, e6 5%.
2 Medium 2.0 The counts are square-rooted, which flattens the odds: d3 about 42%, c4 27%, f5 17%, e6 13%.
1 Easy 8.0 Nearly uniform, so close to a random choice among the moves the search looked at.

The computer plays the best move less often as T rises. Its mistakes still come from the strong network's own shortlist, so they look like plausible but inferior moves rather than blunders.

Why this approach - You ship one model file, and the manifest holds the four temperatures. - Every level costs the same time per move, so all of them fit the 2 s budget. - Strength is tuned with four numbers, with no retraining.

Status: this isn't wired into the app yet. - The model and manifest are in models/, committed in b04b210. // Typed mirror of the `othello-api` crate (see SPEC §4.3). The UI never computes rules:
// it sends these commands and renders the snapshots and events it receives.
//
// Two backends serve the same commands: inside the desktop app they go to the Rust engine through
// Tauri; in a plain browser (the single-file web build) they go to the TypeScript engine in ./engine.
//
// Squares are indices 0..63 (a1 = 0, h8 = 63). Board cells: 0 empty, 1 black, 2 white.

import { invoke } from '@tauri-apps/api/core';
import { listen, type UnlistenFn } from '@tauri-apps/api/event';
import { createWebBackend } from './engine/web-backend.ts';

export type Side = 'black' | 'white';
export type HumanSide = Side | 'random';

export type Mode =
  | { kind: 'vs_computer'; difficulty: number; human: HumanSide }
  | { kind: 'two_players'; black_name?: string | null; white_name?: string | null };

export type Awaiting = 'human' | 'computer' | 'nobody';

export type Status =
  | { state: 'playing' }
  | { state: 'over'; winner: Side | null; resigned: boolean };

export interface Snapshot {
  board: number[];
  to_move: Side;
  awaiting: Awaiting;
  legal: number[];
  last_move: number | null;
  flipped: number[];
  black_count: number;
  white_count: number;
  status: Status;
  mode: Mode;
  can_undo: boolean;
  ply: number;
  history: string[];
}

export type GameEvent =
  | { type: 'state_changed'; snapshot: Snapshot }
  | { type: 'passed'; side: Side }
  | { type: 'thinking'; progress: number }
  | { type: 'game_over'; winner: Side | null; resigned: boolean; black: number; white: number };

export interface Settings {
  show_legal_moves: boolean;
  animations: boolean;
  sound: boolean;
  default_difficulty: number;
  default_human_side: HumanSide;
}

export type ApiError =
  | { code: 'no_game' }
  | { code: 'invalid_difficulty'; given: number }
  | { code: 'game_over' }
  | { code: 'not_your_turn' }
  | { code: 'illegal_move'; square: number }
  | { code: 'nothing_to_undo' }
  | { code: 'hint_unavailable' };

/** True inside the Tauri desktop app. */
const inTauri = typeof window !== 'undefined' && '__TAURI_INTERNALS__' in window;
const web = inTauri ? null : createWebBackend();

export const newGame = (mode: Mode): Promise<Snapshot> => (web ? web.newGame(mode) : invoke('new_game', { mode }));
export const play = (square: number): Promise<Snapshot> => (web ? web.play(square) : invoke('play', { square }));
export const undo = (): Promise<Snapshot> => (web ? web.undo() : invoke('undo'));
export const resign = (): Promise<Snapshot> => (web ? web.resign() : invoke('resign'));
export const snapshot = (): Promise<Snapshot> => (web ? web.snapshot() : invoke('snapshot'));
export const hint = (): Promise<number> => (web ? web.hint() : invoke('hint'));
export const getSettings = (): Promise<Settings> => (web ? web.getSettings() : invoke('get_settings'));
export const setSettings = (settings: Settings): Promise<void> =>
  web ? web.setSettings(settings) : invoke('set_settings', { settings });

/** Subscribe to engine events. Returns the function that unsubscribes. */
export const onGameEvent = (handler: (event: GameEvent) => void): Promise<UnlistenFn> =>
  web
    ? Promise.resolve(web.onEvent(handler))
    : listen<GameEvent>('game-event', (e) => handler(e.payload));

/** "d3" for square 19; "pass" for 64. */
export const squareName = (square: number): string =>
  square === 64 ? 'pass' : 'abcdefgh'[square % 8] + (Math.floor(square / 8) + 1);

  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import * as api from './lib/api';
  import type { GameEvent, HumanSide, Mode, Settings, Side, Snapshot } from './lib/api';
  import Board from './lib/Board.svelte';
  import ChipRain from './lib/ChipRain.svelte';
  import ChipSplash from './lib/ChipSplash.svelte';
  import Icon from './lib/Icon.svelte';
  import Lights from './lib/Lights.svelte';

  type Screen = 'home' | 'setup-computer' | 'setup-two' | 'game' | 'settings' | 'help';

  let screen = $state<Screen>('home');
  let snap = $state<Snapshot | null>(null);
  let settings = $state<Settings>({
    show_legal_moves: true,
    animations: true,
    sound: true,
    default_difficulty: 2,
    default_human_side: 'black'
  });
  let banner = $state('');
  let thinking = $state<number | null>(null);
  let hintSquare = $state<number | null>(null);
  let error = $state('');
  /** Incremented at the start of every game to (re)play the opening chip splash. */
  let splashKey = $state(0);
  let splashing = $state(false);

  // Setup form
  let difficulty = $state(2);
  let human = $state<HumanSide>('black');
  let blackName = $state('');
  let whiteName = $state('');

  const LEVELS = ['Easy', 'Medium', 'Hard', 'Master'];
  const label = (s: Side) => (s === 'black' ? 'Black' : 'White');
  const other = (s: Side): Side => (s === 'black' ? 'white' : 'black');

  let bannerTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

  function playerName(s: Side): string {
    if (!snap) return label(s);
    if (snap.mode.kind === 'two_players') {
      return (s === 'black' ? snap.mode.black_name : snap.mode.white_name) || label(s);
    }
    return snap.mode.human === s ? `${label(s)} (you)` : `${label(s)} (computer)`;
  }

  function onEvent(e: GameEvent) {
    if (e.type === 'state_changed') {
      snap = e.snapshot;
      hintSquare = null;
      if (e.snapshot.awaiting !== 'computer') thinking = null;
    } else if (e.type === 'passed') {
      banner = `${label(e.side)} has no legal move — ${label(other(e.side))} plays again`;
      clearTimeout(bannerTimer);
      bannerTimer = setTimeout(() => (banner = ''), 3500);
    } else if (e.type === 'thinking') {
      thinking = e.progress;
    }
  }

  async function run<T>(action: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T | undefined> {
    error = '';
    try {
      return await action();
    } catch (err) {
      error = typeof err === 'object' && err && 'code' in err ? String((err as { code: string }).code) : String(err);
      return undefined;
    }
  }

    banner = '';
    const s = await run(() => api.newGame(mode));
    if (s) {
      snap = s;
      screen = 'game';
      if (settings.animations) {
        splashKey += 1;
        splashing = true;
      }

  }

  const startTwo = () => start({ kind: 'two_players', black_name: blackName || null, white_name: whiteName || null });

    if (!snap || snap.awaiting !== 'human' || !snap.legal.includes(i)) return;
    const s = await run(() => api.play(i));
    if (s) snap = s;
  }

  async function doUndo() {
    const s = await run(api.undo);
    if (s) snap = s;
  }

  async function doResign() {
    const s = await run(api.resign);

  }

  async function doHint() {
    const sq = await run(api.hint);
    if (sq !== undefined) hintSquare = sq;
  }

    if (!snap) return;
    const m = snap.mode;

      );
    }

<!-- The board: walnut frame with chasing marquee bulbs, oak squares, glossy 3D discs.
     It only renders the snapshot it is given; all rules live in the engine. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { squareName, type Snapshot } from './api';

  let {
    snap,
    showLegal,
    hintSquare,
    onSquare
  }: {
    snap: Snapshot;
    showLegal: boolean;
    hintSquare: number | null;
    onSquare: (square: number) => void;
  } = $props();

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => i);

  // Flips ripple outward from the placed disc: --ring is the distance (in squares) minus one;
  // CSS turns it into a delay using the timings in design.md (section 12).
  function ring(i: number): number {
    if (snap.last_move === null || !snap.flipped.includes(i)) return 0;
    const dr = Math.abs(Math.floor(i / 8) - Math.floor(snap.last_move / 8));
    const dc = Math.abs((i % 8) - (snap.last_move % 8));
    return Math.max(dr, dc) - 1;
  }

  const describe = (i: number, cell: number) =>
    `${squareName(i)}${cell === 1 ? ', black' : cell === 2 ? ', white' : ', empty'}`;
</script>

/** Time budget for the strongest level, in milliseconds. */

export interface RankedMove {
  move: number;
  /** Search value for the side to move; higher is better. Only differences are meaningful. */
  score: number;
}

/**
 * Every legal placement scored by a full-window search, best first (equal scores keep square order).
 * Unlike `chooseMove` nothing is pruned at the root, so each move gets its true value at this depth.
 * Positions with few empty squares are searched to the end of the game. Deterministic.
 */
export function rankMoves(position: Position, depth = 4): RankedMove[] {
  const b = toBoard(position);
  const me = code(position.toMove);
  let empties = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) if (b[i] === 0) empties++;
  const plies = empties <= 6 ? 64 : depth;
  const clock = { nodes: 0, deadline: Infinity };
  const ranked = movesOf(b, me).map((move) => ({
    move,
    score: -negamax(play(b, move, me, flipsAt(b, move, me)), 3 - me, plies - 1, -Infinity, Infinity, false, clock)
  }));
  return ranked.sort((x, y) => y.score - x.score || x.move - y.move);
}

// Post-game review: replay a finished game and, for every move the human played, say whether it was
// among the moves the computer itself would have chosen from the same position.
//
// The computer's opinion of a position is a ranked list of moves, each with a probability. A move is
// "good" if it is in the top-k moves OR inside the top-p nucleus (the shortest prefix of the list whose
// probabilities add up to p); the single best move is "best". Moves that are the only legal move are
// "forced" and left out of the score.
//
// Where the opinion comes from is pluggable (`Analyzer`). Today it is the web build's alpha-beta search
// with a softmax over the move values; once Oroletto is wired in, the analyzer will return its MCTS root
// visit shares instead, and nothing else here changes.

import { rankMoves, type RankedMove } from './ai.ts';
import { PASS, Position, parseMove, type Side } from './position.ts';

/** A move counts as good when it is among the computer's top K moves… */
export const REVIEW_TOP_K = 3;
/** …or inside the smallest set of its best moves whose probabilities add up to this. */
export const REVIEW_TOP_P = 0.2;
/** Softmax temperature turning search values into probabilities (value units: roughly one disc). */
export const REVIEW_TEMPERATURE = 12;

export interface Candidate {
  move: number;
  score: number;
  /** The computer's chance of choosing this move; the candidates of a position add up to 1. */
  prob: number;
  /** 1 = best. Moves with equal scores share a rank. */
  rank: number;
}

export type Verdict = 'best' | 'good' | 'miss' | 'forced';

export interface Feedback {
  verdict: Verdict;
  played: Candidate;
  /** Every legal move, best first. */
  candidates: Candidate[];
  /** The moves that would have been accepted (top-k plus the top-p nucleus), best first. */
  accepted: Candidate[];
}

export type Analyzer = (position: Position) => RankedMove[] | Promise<RankedMove[]>;

export interface JudgeOptions {
  k?: number;
  p?: number;
  temperature?: number;
}

/** Turn ranked values into candidates with probabilities (softmax) and competition ranks. */
export function toCandidates(ranked: RankedMove[], temperature = REVIEW_TEMPERATURE): Candidate[] {
  const sorted = ranked.slice().sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.move - b.move);
  if (sorted.length === 0) return [];
  const top = sorted[0].score;
  const weights = sorted.map((r) => Math.exp((r.score - top) / temperature));
  const total = weights.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  return sorted.map((r, i) => ({
    move: r.move,
    score: r.score,
    prob: weights[i] / total,
    rank: 1 + sorted.filter((o) => o.score > r.score).length
  }));
}

/** Judge one move against the computer's ranked opinion of the position it was played in. */
export function judge(ranked: RankedMove[], played: number, options: JudgeOptions = {}): Feedback {
  const { k = REVIEW_TOP_K, p = REVIEW_TOP_P, temperature = REVIEW_TEMPERATURE } = options;
  const candidates = toCandidates(ranked, temperature);
  const mine = candidates.find((c) => c.move === played);
  if (!mine) throw new Error(`move ${played} is not among the legal moves`);

  // Top-k by rank (ties at the boundary stay in), plus the nucleus of probability mass p.
  const inTopK = candidates.filter((c) => c.rank <= k);
  let mass = 0;
  let cut = 0;
  while (cut < candidates.length && mass < p) mass += candidates[cut++].prob;
  const lastScore = cut > 0 ? candidates[cut - 1].score : -Infinity;
  const inNucleus = candidates.filter((c, i) => i < cut || c.score === lastScore);
  const accepted = candidates.filter((c) => inTopK.includes(c) || inNucleus.includes(c));

  const verdict: Verdict =
    candidates.length === 1 ? 'forced' : mine.rank === 1 ? 'best' : accepted.includes(mine) ? 'good' : 'miss';
  return { verdict, played: mine, candidates, accepted };
}

  ply: number;
  mover: Side;

// Drives the web session the way the UI does: commands in, snapshots and events out.

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import type { GameEvent, Mode, Snapshot } from '../api.ts';
import { Rng, chooseMove, greedyBest } from './ai.ts';
import { PASS, Position, parseMove, type Side } from './position.ts';
import { WebSession } from './session.ts';

const sq = (name: string) => parseMove(name)!;
const twoPlayers: Mode = { kind: 'two_players' };
const vs = (human: 'black' | 'white' | 'random', difficulty: number): Mode => ({ kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty, human });

function make(opts: ConstructorParameters<typeof WebSession>[0] = {}) {
  const session = new WebSession({ seed: 1, minThinkMs: 5, level4BudgetMs: 40, ...opts });
  const events: GameEvent[] = [];
  session.onEvent((e) => events.push(e));
  /** Wait until a state_changed satisfying `pred` has arrived (or time out). */
  const waitState = async (pred: (s: Snapshot) => boolean, ms = 4000): Promise<Snapshot> => {
    const end = Date.now() + ms;
    for (;;) {
      const hit = events.find((e) => e.type === 'state_changed' && pred(e.snapshot));
      if (hit && hit.type === 'state_changed') return hit.snapshot;
      if (Date.now() > end) throw new Error('timed out waiting for a state');
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5));
    }
  };
  return { session, events, waitState };
}

const rejects = (fn: () => unknown, code: string) =>
  assert.throws(fn, (e: any) => e && e.code === code, `expected ${code}`);

test('commands fail before a game exists', () => {
  const { session } = make();
  rejects(() => session.snapshot(), 'no_game');
  rejects(() => session.play(19), 'no_game');
  rejects(() => session.undo(), 'no_game');
  rejects(() => session.resign(), 'no_game');

// Post-game review: judging a move against the computer's ranked opinion, and replaying whole games.
// Run with:  npm test

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import { Rng, rankMoves, type RankedMove } from './ai.ts';
import { PASS, Position, moveName, parseMove, type Side } from './position.ts';
import { REVIEW_TOP_K, REVIEW_TOP_P, judge, reviewGame, toCandidates } from './review.ts';

const ranked = (scores: number[]): RankedMove[] => scores.map((score, i) => ({ move: 10 + i, score }));

/** Play a whole game; `chooser` picks the move for each side. Returns the move names. */
function playGame(chooser: (pos: Position, side: Side) => number): string[] {
  const names: string[] = [];
  let pos = Position.initial();
  while (!pos.isTerminal()) {
    const side = pos.toMove;
    const legal = pos.legalMoves();
    const move = legal.length === 1 ? legal[0] : chooser(pos, side);
    names.push(moveName(move));
    pos = pos.play(move).position;
  }
  return names;
}

test('the defaults are top-3 and top-p 0.2', () => {
  assert.equal(REVIEW_TOP_K, 3);
  assert.equal(REVIEW_TOP_P, 0.2);
});

test('probabilities sum to one, best first, and equal scores share a rank', () => {
  const c = toCandidates(ranked([10, 40, 40, 5]));
  assert.deepEqual(c.map((x) => x.score), [40, 40, 10, 5]);
  assert.deepEqual(c.map((x) => x.rank), [1, 1, 3, 4]);
  assert.ok(Math.abs(c.reduce((s, x) => s + x.prob, 0) - 1) < 1e-12);
  assert.ok(c[0].prob === c[1].prob && c[1].prob > c[2].prob && c[2].prob > c[3].prob);
});

test('best, good (top 3) and miss', () => {
  const r = ranked([50, 40, 30, 10, 0]);
  assert.equal(judge(r, 10).verdict, 'best');
  assert.equal(judge(r, 11).verdict, 'good');
  assert.equal(judge(r, 12).verdict, 'good');
  assert.equal(judge(r, 13).verdict, 'miss');
  assert.equal(judge(r, 14).verdict, 'miss');
  assert.deepEqual(judge(r, 14).accepted.map((c) => c.move), [10, 11, 12]);
  assert.equal(judge(r, 13).played.rank, 4);
});

test('a lone legal move is forced', () => {
  const f = judge(ranked([7]), 10);
  assert.equal(f.verdict, 'forced');
  assert.equal(f.played.prob, 1);
});

test('a move tied with the best is best, and ties at the cut-off are kept', () => {
  assert.equal(judge(ranked([30, 30, 30, 30, 0]), 13).verdict, 'best');
  // 4th and 5th share rank 3: both are inside the top-3 by rank.
  const r = ranked([50, 40, 20, 20, 0]);
  assert.equal(judge(r, 13).verdict, 'good');
});

test('the top-p nucleus accepts a move that top-k alone would not', () => {
  // 25 moves with nearly equal values: each gets about 4%, so 20% of the mass needs five moves.
  const flat = ranked(Array.from({ length: 25 }, (_, i) => 100 - i * 0.1));
  assert.equal(judge(flat, 14).verdict, 'good'); // 5th place, outside top-3
  assert.equal(judge(flat, 14, { p: 0.0001 }).verdict, 'miss'); // without the nucleus
  assert.equal(judge(flat, 20).verdict, 'miss'); // 11th place is outside both
});

test('judging a move that was not legal is an error', () => {
  assert.throws(() => judge(ranked([5, 4]), 99), /not among the legal moves/);

  edge follows.
- **Textures** live in `ui/public/textures/` (`wood.jpg`, `red-velvet.jpg`, `green-velvet.jpg`).
  To use your own, drop a PNG or JPG there and point a token at it, e.g.
  `url(/textures/my-felt.jpg) center / cover`.
- Don't rename or delete tokens: the app reads them by name. The build fails if the code uses a
  token that is missing here, and warns if a token here is not used by anything.
- Colours with transparency: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`. Multi-layer values (a gradient over a
  texture) separate layers with commas; the first layer is on top.
- Speeds are durations: **bigger = slower**. To make something static, set a huge duration
  (`9999s`). To switch all motion off, use Settings > Animations in the app.

Sections go from the outside in: neon lights, the room, border lighting, text, brass and velvet, buttons,
icon buttons, option boxes, scoreboard, board frame, bulbs, board surface, discs, disc
animations, hints, banners and dialogs, poker chips, the roulette wheel.

## 18. Poker chips (start-of-game splash and win rain)

At the start of every game chips fly in from the edges and splash across the screen, bounce
and fade. When someone wins, chips rain from the top while the result dialog is open. Both
are switched off by Settings > Animations.

```tokens
chip_colors: #b3202a, #1f8a46, #1f3f9a, #17171a, #d9a521, #6a2a8c   # comma separated: red, green, blue, black, gold, purple
chip_notch: #f6f0e4                       # the white notches round the edge
chip_size: 54px
chip_splash_count: 34                     # chips in the opening splash (a plain number, no unit)
chip_splash_duration: 2.8s                # how long the splash lasts (a number of seconds, ends in s)
overlay_bg: rgba(10, 3, 1, 0.72)          # dimming behind the dialog
overlay_blur: 3px
```

<!-- Post-game review: step through the finished game from the first move to the last. On each of your
     moves you get a verdict: was it among the moves the computer would have played from there?
     The judging itself lives in engine/review.ts; this component only shows it. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import { squareName, type Side, type Snapshot } from './api';
  import Board, { type Mark } from './Board.svelte';
  import Icon from './Icon.svelte';
  import { PASS, Position } from './engine/position';
  import { REVIEW_TOP_K, REVIEW_TOP_P, reviewGame, type Review, type ReviewStep, type Verdict } from './engine/review';

  let { snap, onclose }: { snap: Snapshot; onclose: () => void } = $props();

  const human: Side = snap.mode.kind === 'vs_computer' ? (snap.mode.human as Side) : 'black';
  const label = (s: Side) => (s === 'black' ? 'Black' : 'White');
  const pct = (x: number) => `${Math.round(x * 100)}%`;

  let review = $state<Review | null>(null);
  let progress = $state({ done: 0, total: 0 });
  let failed = $state('');
  /** 0 = the starting position; n = after move n. */
  let index = $state(0);

  onMount(() => {
    let stop = false;
    reviewGame(snap.history, human, {
      onProgress: (done, total) => (progress = { done, total }),
      cancelled: () => stop
    })
      .then((r) => {
        if (r && !stop) review = r;
      })
      .catch((e) => (failed = String(e?.message ?? e)));
    return () => (stop = true);
  });

  const steps = $derived(review?.steps ?? []);
  const step = $derived<ReviewStep | null>(index > 0 ? (steps[index - 1] ?? null) : null);
  const position = $derived(step ? step.after : Position.initial());
  const last = $derived(steps.length);
  const judgedSteps = $derived(steps.filter((s) => s.feedback));

  /** The board as the Board component expects it (a snapshot of a game that is not being played). */
  const view = $derived.by<Snapshot>(() => {
    const board = Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => {
      const bit = 1n << BigInt(i);
      return position.black & bit ? 1 : position.white & bit ? 2 : 0;
    });
    const { black, white } = position.counts();
    return {
      board,
      to_move: position.toMove,
      awaiting: 'nobody',
      legal: [],
      last_move: step && step.move !== PASS ? step.move : null,
      flipped: step?.flipped ?? [],
      black_count: black,
      white_count: white,
      status: { state: 'playing' },
      mode: snap.mode,
      can_undo: false,
      ply: index,
      history: snap.history.slice(0, index)
    };
  });

  const PLAYED_BADGE: Record<Verdict, string> = { best: '★', good: '✓', miss: '✗', forced: '•' };

  /** Badges: your move's verdict, and the computer's favourite squares numbered by rank. */
  const marks = $derived.by<Record<number, Mark>>(() => {
    const f = step?.feedback;
    if (!f) return {};
    const out: Record<number, Mark> = {};
    for (const c of f.accepted) out[c.move] = { text: String(c.rank), kind: 'suggest' };
    out[f.played.move] = {
      text: PLAYED_BADGE[f.verdict],
      kind: f.verdict === 'forced' ? 'good' : f.verdict
    };
    return out;
  });

  const go = (i: number) => (index = Math.max(0, Math.min(last, i)));
  const missIndexes = $derived(steps.flatMap((s, i) => (s.feedback?.verdict === 'miss' ? [i + 1] : [])));
  const nextMiss = $derived(missIndexes.find((i) => i > index) ?? null);

  function onKey(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    if (!review || e.altKey || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) return;
    const key = e.key;
    if (key === 'ArrowRight') go(index + 1);
    else if (key === 'ArrowLeft') go(index - 1);
    else if (key === 'Home') go(0);
    else if (key === 'End') go(last);
    else if (key === 'Escape') return onclose();
    else return;
    e.preventDefault();
  }

  const names = (cs: { move: number; rank: number; prob: number }[]) =>
    cs.map((c) => `${squareName(c.move)} (${pct(c.prob)})`).join(', ');

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch Othello Player in development mode:  bash launch.sh
# (--check only verifies the prerequisites and exits.)
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Pick up toolchains installed by rustup and nvm, which only add themselves to
# interactive shells' PATH.
[ -d "$HOME/.cargo/bin" ] && export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -s "$HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  . "$HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh"
fi

missing=0
need() { # need <command> <how to get it>
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Missing: $1. $2" >&2
    missing=1
  fi
}
need cargo "Install Rust: https://rustup.rs"
need node "Install Node.js (an LTS release), e.g. with nvm: https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm"
need npm "It comes with Node.js."
[ "$missing" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
  echo "OK: cargo $(cargo --version | cut -d' ' -f2), node $(node --version), npm $(npm --version)"
  exit 0
fi

if [ ! -d "$ROOT/ui/node_modules" ]; then
  echo "Installing UI dependencies (first run)..."
  (cd "$ROOT/ui" && npm install)
fi

# The first launch compiles the Rust side and takes a minute or two.
cd "$ROOT/app"
exec npx --prefix ../ui tauri dev

1	# Putting the game on your GitHub Pages site
2	
3	Two files do everything:
4	
5	| File | What it is |
6	|---|---|
7	| `web/othello.html` | the whole game (one self-contained page, no other files needed) |
8	| `web/embed/play-button.html` | a "Play Othello" button that opens the game inside your page |
9	
10	## Steps
11	
12	1. **Upload the game.** In your site's repository, make a folder (say `othello/`) and put a copy of
13	   `web/othello.html` in it, named `index.html` → `othello/index.html`.
14	2. **Add the button.** Open the page of your site where the Play button should appear and paste the
15	   contents of `web/embed/play-button.html` where you want it. If that page is not in the same folder
16	   as `othello/`, change `data-src` in the button to the path from that page to the game.
17	3. **Publish.** Commit and push your site's repository. GitHub Pages updates in about a minute.
18	4. **Try it.** Hard-refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R), click the button, and play a move.
19	
20	## If something is off
21	
22	- **"404" or a blank frame:** `data-src` is wrong. It is relative to the page holding the button.
23	  For a project site at `username.github.io/repo/` do not start the path with `/`.
24	- **You still see the old game after an update:** hard-refresh; browsers cache the file.
25	- **You added `sandbox` to the iframe:** it needs `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` or the game cannot run.
26	
27	## Updating the game later
28	
29	Rebuild with `cd ui && npm run build:web` (this rewrites `web/othello.html`), copy the new file over
30	`othello/index.html` in your site, and push.

// Orolleto, the card-room dealer: what he says and how he looks at each moment of a game.
// Pure functions of the game state (plus a random source, so tests can pin the choice).

import type { Snapshot } from './api';

export type Mood = 'idle' | 'think' | 'happy' | 'sad';
export interface Line {
  say: string;
  mood: Mood;
}

export const DEALER_NAME = 'Orolleto';

type Rng = () => number;
const pick = <T>(items: readonly T[], rng: Rng): T => items[Math.min(items.length - 1, Math.floor(rng() * items.length))];

const CORNERS = [0, 7, 56, 63];

const WELCOME = [
  "Welcome to the table. I'm Orolleto. Place your discs!",
  'Cards are dealt, discs are cut. Your move, friend.',
  'The house is open. Show me what you have.'
];
const WELCOME_TWO = ['Two players, one table. May the best disc win.', 'A friendly hand! I will keep the score.'];
const THINKING = ['Hmm, let me think…', 'Studying the felt…', 'One moment, I am counting discs…', 'Interesting. Very interesting…'];
const COMPUTER_CORNER = ['A corner. The house will take that.', 'Corner secured. House rules.'];
const COMPUTER_BIG = ['Count them: that is a big flip!', 'Turn them over, all of them.'];
const COMPUTER_PLAIN = ['Your turn.', 'The house plays.', 'Your move, friend.', "Let's see you answer that."];
const HUMAN_CORNER = ['A corner! Nicely played.', 'Ooh, you took a corner. I felt that.'];
const HUMAN_BIG = ['Whoa, that is a lot of discs!', 'Careful, you are cleaning me out.'];
const PASS_HUMAN = ['No move for you, so I play again.'];
const PASS_COMPUTER = ['I have to pass! Go again, friend.'];
const WIN = ['You cleaned me out! Take a bow.', 'The house pays out. Well played!'];
const LOSS = ['The house always wins… this time.', 'Better luck next hand, friend.'];
const DRAW = ['A push! Honours even.'];
const REVIEW_BEST = ['Perfect read. That is what I would play.', 'Spot on!'];
const REVIEW_GOOD = ['Solid. A good player sees that.', 'A fine choice.'];
const REVIEW_MISS = ['Ah, that one cost you a little.', 'Hmm, I would have looked elsewhere.'];
const REVIEW_FORCED = ['No choice there, friend.'];

export const welcome = (twoPlayers: boolean, rng: Rng = Math.random): Line => ({
  say: pick(twoPlayers ? WELCOME_TWO : WELCOME, rng),
  mood: 'happy'
});

export const thinking = (rng: Rng = Math.random): Line => ({ say: pick(THINKING, rng), mood: 'think' });

export const passed = (humanPassed: boolean, rng: Rng = Math.random): Line => ({
  say: pick(humanPassed ? PASS_HUMAN : PASS_COMPUTER, rng),
  mood: humanPassed ? 'happy' : 'sad'
});

/** How the dealer reacts when the game moves from `prev` to `next`; null to stay quiet. */
export function reactToMove(prev: Snapshot | null, next: Snapshot, rng: Rng = Math.random): Line | null {
  if (!prev || next.mode.kind !== 'vs_computer' || next.ply <= prev.ply || next.last_move === null) return null;
  if (next.status.state === 'over') return null; // the result has its own line
  const mover = next.board[next.last_move] === 1 ? 'black' : 'white';
  const byHuman = mover === next.mode.human;
  const corner = CORNERS.includes(next.last_move);
  const big = next.flipped.length >= 5;
  if (byHuman) {
    if (corner) return { say: pick(HUMAN_CORNER, rng), mood: 'sad' };
    if (big) return { say: pick(HUMAN_BIG, rng), mood: 'sad' };
    return null;
  }
  if (corner) return { say: pick(COMPUTER_CORNER, rng), mood: 'happy' };
  if (big) return { say: pick(COMPUTER_BIG, rng), mood: 'happy' };
  return rng() < 0.4 ? { say: pick(COMPUTER_PLAIN, rng), mood: 'idle' } : null;
}

/** The dealer's line when a game ends. */
export function reactToEnd(snap: Snapshot, rng: Rng = Math.random): Line {
  if (snap.status.state !== 'over' || snap.status.winner === null) return { say: pick(DRAW, rng), mood: 'idle' };
  if (snap.mode.kind !== 'vs_computer') return { say: pick(WIN, rng), mood: 'happy' };
  return snap.status.winner === snap.mode.human
    ? { say: pick(WIN, rng), mood: 'sad' }
    : { say: pick(LOSS, rng), mood: 'happy' };
}

// Orolleto's reactions. Run with:  npm test

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import type { Snapshot } from './api.ts';
import { reactToEnd, reactToMove, reviewLine, thinking, welcome } from './dealer.ts';

const always = (x: number) => () => x;

/** A snapshot of a game where `human` plays and `square` was just placed by `by`. */
function snap(opts: { ply: number; square: number | null; by?: 'black' | 'white'; flips?: number; over?: 'human' | 'computer' | 'draw' }): Snapshot {
  const board = Array<number>(64).fill(0);
  if (opts.square !== null) board[opts.square] = opts.by === 'white' ? 2 : 1;
  const winner = opts.over === 'human' ? 'black' : opts.over === 'computer' ? 'white' : null;
  return {
    board,
    to_move: 'black',
    awaiting: 'human',
    legal: [],
    last_move: opts.square,
    flipped: Array.from({ length: opts.flips ?? 1 }, (_, i) => 20 + i),
    black_count: 2,
    white_count: 2,
    status: opts.over ? { state: 'over', winner, resigned: false } : { state: 'playing' },
    mode: { kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty: 2, human: 'black' },
    can_undo: false,
    ply: opts.ply,
    history: []
  };
}

test('he welcomes players differently in one- and two-player games', () => {
  assert.notEqual(welcome(false, always(0)).say, welcome(true, always(0)).say);
  assert.equal(welcome(false).mood, 'happy');
});

test('while the computer thinks he looks thoughtful', () => {
  assert.equal(thinking().mood, 'think');
});

test('he stays quiet without a new move, and in two-player games', () => {
  const a = snap({ ply: 3, square: 19 });
  assert.equal(reactToMove(a, a), null);
  assert.equal(reactToMove(null, a), null);
  const two = { ...snap({ ply: 4, square: 0, by: 'black' }), mode: { kind: 'two_players' } } as Snapshot;
  assert.equal(reactToMove(snap({ ply: 3, square: 19 }), two), null);
});

test('he admires the player\'s corner and big flips, and is silent on ordinary moves', () => {
  const prev = snap({ ply: 2, square: 19 });
  const corner = reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 3, square: 7, by: 'black' }), always(0));
  assert.ok(corner && /corner/i.test(corner.say) && corner.mood === 'sad');
  const big = reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 3, square: 27, by: 'black', flips: 6 }), always(0));
  assert.ok(big && big.mood === 'sad');
  assert.equal(reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 3, square: 27, by: 'black', flips: 2 }), always(0)), null);
});

test('he gloats about the computer\'s corner and sometimes comments on its other moves', () => {
  const prev = snap({ ply: 3, square: 19 });
  const corner = reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 4, square: 63, by: 'white' }), always(0));
  assert.ok(corner && /corner/i.test(corner.say) && corner.mood === 'happy');
  assert.ok(reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 4, square: 27, by: 'white' }), always(0.1))); // < 0.4: comments
  assert.equal(reactToMove(prev, snap({ ply: 4, square: 27, by: 'white' }), always(0.9)), null);
});

test('the result line depends on who won', () => {
  assert.equal(reactToEnd(snap({ ply: 60, square: 1, over: 'human' }), always(0)).mood, 'sad');
  assert.equal(reactToEnd(snap({ ply: 60, square: 1, over: 'computer' }), always(0)).mood, 'happy');
  assert.equal(reactToEnd(snap({ ply: 60, square: 1, over: 'draw' }), always(0)).mood, 'idle');
});

test('he comments on every kind of reviewed move', () => {
  assert.equal(reviewLine('best').mood, 'happy');
  assert.equal(reviewLine('good').mood, 'happy');
  assert.equal(reviewLine('miss').mood, 'sad');
  assert.equal(reviewLine('forced').mood, 'idle');
});

<!-- Start of a game: poker chips are thrown in from the bottom and the sides, arc across the
     screen, land, bounce and fade. Counts, colours, size and timing come from design.md (section 17).
     Calls `ondone` when the last chip has faded so the parent can remove it. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';

  let { ondone }: { ondone?: () => void } = $props();

  const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const COLORS = css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-colors').split(',').map((c) => c.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const COUNT = Math.max(0, Number.parseInt(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-splash-count'), 10) || 0);
  const DURATION = Number.parseFloat(css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-splash-duration')) || 2.8; // seconds
  const VALUES = ['5', '10', '25', '50', '100', '500'];
  const MAX_DELAY = 0.7;

  const rand = (min: number, max: number) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);

  // Launch points: bottom-left corner, bottom-centre, bottom-right corner (all just off screen).
  const ORIGINS = [
    { x: -6, y: 104 },
    { x: 50, y: 110 },
    { x: 106, y: 104 }
  ];

  const chips = Array.from({ length: COUNT }, (_, i) => {
    const o = ORIGINS[i % ORIGINS.length];
    const tx = rand(5, 95);
    const ty = rand(10, 88);
    return {
      color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] ?? '#b3202a',
      value: VALUES[i % VALUES.length],
      sx: o.x, sy: o.y,
      mx: (o.x + tx) / 2 + rand(-8, 8),
      my: Math.min(o.y, ty) - rand(14, 32),
      tx, ty,
      r1: rand(-300, 300),
      r2: rand(-540, 540),
      tilt: rand(0, 1) < 0.5 ? -1 : 1,
      delay: (i / Math.max(COUNT, 1)) * MAX_DELAY + rand(0, 0.12),
      scale: rand(0.85, 1.25)
    };
  });

  onMount(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => ondone?.(), (DURATION + MAX_DELAY + 0.4) * 1000);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  });
</script>

<div class="splash" aria-hidden="true">

             --r1:{c.r1}deg; --r2:{c.r2}deg; --delay:{c.delay}s; --k:{c.scale}"

<!-- Start of a game: poker chips burst across the screen three times. In each burst a ring of chips
     rushes in from beyond the edges to the middle of the table, then flies straight back out.
     Counts, colours, size and timing come from design.md (section 18).
     Calls `ondone` when the last chip has left so the parent can remove it. -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';

  let { ondone }: { ondone?: () => void } = $props();

  const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const num = (name: string, fallback: number) => Number.parseFloat(css.getPropertyValue(name)) || fallback;
  const COLORS = css.getPropertyValue('--d-chip-colors').split(',').map((c) => c.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const PER_BURST = Math.max(0, Math.round(num('--d-chip-splash-count', 24)));
  const BURSTS = Math.max(1, Math.round(num('--d-chip-splash-bursts', 3)));
  const DURATION = num('--d-chip-splash-duration', 2.2); // seconds for one burst (in and out)
  const GAP = num('--d-chip-splash-burst-gap', 0.8); // seconds between the starts of two bursts
  const VALUES = ['5', '10', '25', '50', '100', '500'];
  const JITTER = 0.25; // chips of one burst do not leave in perfect lockstep

  const rand = (min: number, max: number) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);

  // Positions are percentages of the viewport, measured from its centre. A radius of 62 is beyond
  // every edge (the half-width is 50), so chips enter and leave out of sight.
  const EDGE = 64;
  const point = (angle: number, radius: number) => ({
    x: 50 + Math.cos(angle) * radius,
    y: 50 + Math.sin(angle) * radius
  });

  const chips = Array.from({ length: BURSTS * PER_BURST }, (_, i) => {
    const burst = Math.floor(i / PER_BURST);
    const n = i % PER_BURST;
    // Spread each burst evenly round the circle; each burst is turned a little from the last.
    const angle = (n / PER_BURST) * Math.PI * 2 + burst * 0.4 + rand(-0.12, 0.12);
    const start = point(angle, EDGE + rand(0, 6));
    const mid = point(angle, rand(1, 7));
    const out = point(angle + rand(-0.05, 0.05), EDGE + rand(2, 10));
    return {
      color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] ?? '#b3202a',
      value: VALUES[i % VALUES.length],
      sx: start.x, sy: start.y,
      mx: mid.x, my: mid.y,
      ox: out.x, oy: out.y,
      r1: rand(-360, 360),
      r2: rand(-720, 720),
      tilt: Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1,
      delay: burst * GAP + rand(0, JITTER),
      scale: rand(0.85, 1.25)
    };
  });

  onMount(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => ondone?.(), ((BURSTS - 1) * GAP + JITTER + DURATION + 0.3) * 1000);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  });
</script>

import json, base64, subprocess, time, sys, urllib.request, os
PORT = 4455
gd = subprocess.Popen(['/snap/bin/geckodriver', '--port', str(PORT)], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
time.sleep(1.5)
BASE = f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}'
def call(method, path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, method=method, data=json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode(), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60))['value']
sess = call('POST', '/session', {'capabilities': {'alwaysMatch': {'browserName': 'firefox', 'moz:firefoxOptions': {'args': ['-headless', '-profile', os.path.expanduser('~/othello-ff-profile')]}}}})
sid = sess['sessionId']
S = f'/session/{sid}'
OUT = os.path.expanduser('~/othello-shots')
def shot(name):
    png = call('GET', S + '/screenshot')
    open(f'{OUT}/{name}.png', 'wb').write(base64.b64decode(png))
def js(script, *args):
    return call('POST', S + '/execute/sync', {'script': script, 'args': list(args)})
def size(w, h):
    call('POST', S + '/window/rect', {'width': w, 'height': h})
def click_text(text):
    return js("const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b=>b.textContent.trim()===arguments[0]); if(!b) return false; b.click(); return true;", text)
try:
    exec(open(sys.argv[1]).read())
finally:
    try: call('DELETE', S)
    except Exception: pass
    gd.terminate()
EOF

### 3.6 Look and design tokens
- One look, a **casino card room**: mahogany wood background and frames, burnished brass rims, **red velvet** button faces with brass rims and round icon buttons (Home, Undo, Hint, Resign, New game), a **green felt** board with grid lines (the same green velvet covers the scoreboard panels, option boxes and result dialog), flat-ish buttons with a thin 3D edge (tunable via `button_depth` and `button_bevel`), glossy black and white discs, a neon-sign title, a plain wood background lit only by an **RGB LED strip** round the window edge (individually coloured bulbs with their own glow, a colour pattern flowing clockwise, two interleaved sets twinkling like the board's marquee bulbs; no vignette or other effects), chasing marquee bulbs on the board frame, and a slow roulette wheel on the home screen.
- **Chip animations:** at the start of every game poker chips are thrown in from the bottom and sides, arc across the screen, land, bounce and fade (about 3 s, never blocks play). When someone wins, chips rain from the top while the result dialog is open (not when you lose to the computer).
- Every colour, texture and timing is a **design token** in the repo-root `design.md`. A Vite plugin turns them into CSS variables, reloads the dev app when the file changes, fails the build if the code uses an undefined token, and warns about unused ones. Textures live in `ui/public/textures/`.
- Board details: discs on a 3D rotor (drop on placement, flips that ripple outward from the new disc and rise as they turn), pulsing rings on legal squares, a frame on the last move.
- **Responsive layout:** every screen fits the window with no scrolling down to the minimum 480x600. The game screen is a grid whose board is sized from both the width and the height left over (so it is never cut off or too big); in wide windows (aspect ratio of 5:4 or wider) the board sits on the left and the scoreboard, controls and move list form a column on the right; the move list is dropped in very short windows. Notices (pass banner, errors) float over the page so they never move the board. Content keeps clear of the LED strip.
- All motion respects Settings > Animations and `prefers-reduced-motion`. Hints are rings and frames, not colour alone.

### 3.7 Web build
- A **single self-contained HTML page** (`web/othello.html`, built by `npm run build:web`) runs the same UI in a browser, for hosting on GitHub Pages or anywhere else. No server or network is needed.
- The UI talks to a backend through `ui/src/lib/api.ts`: inside Tauri that is the Rust engine; in a browser it is a **TypeScript port** of the engine and session (`ui/src/lib/engine/`), with settings in localStorage. The port is verified against the same golden data as the Rust engine and has the same session behaviour (automatic passes, undo rules, stale computer moves discarded).
- The browser build has no neural network, so its four levels are classic bots: random, greedy, alpha-beta depth 3, and time-limited iterative-deepening alpha-beta (about 0.9 s). Oroletto stays desktop-only unless an in-browser model runtime is added later.
- The page is generated: rebuild it after any UI or `design.md` change.

### 3.7 Game review and the dealer
- **Review (vs computer only).** The result dialog offers "Review game": the finished game is replayed from the first move to the last (buttons, arrow keys, Home/End, a strip of your moves, "Next miss"). Each of your moves gets a verdict against the computer's own ranking of the moves from that position: **best** (its first choice), **good** (in its **top-3** moves, or inside the **top-p = 0.2** probability nucleus), **missed** (neither), or **forced** (only legal move; not scored). Board badges mark your move and the computer's favourite squares; a summary shows the share of your moves that matched. Passes and the computer's moves are replayed but not judged.
- The ranking comes from a pluggable analyzer (`ui/src/lib/engine/review.ts`). Until Oroletto is wired in it is the web build's alpha-beta search (every legal move scored at depth 4, exact in the last 6 squares) turned into probabilities with a softmax; with Oroletto it becomes the MCTS root visit shares, and nothing else changes. k, p and the softmax temperature are constants in that file.
- **Orolleto**, the card-room dealer (an SVG character in a green eyeshade and red bow tie, coloured by `design.md` section 21), greets you on the home screen, comments during games against the computer (thinking, corners, big flips, passes, the result) and comments on each reviewed move. His moods (idle, thinking, happy, sad) and his animations obey Settings > Animations.

// Orolleto, the card-room dealer: decides what he says and how he looks at each moment of the app.
// The lines themselves live in dialogues.ts; this file chooses among them.
//
// Two kinds of randomness shape what you see:
//  - which line: picked at random from a big pool, never one he said recently;
//  - whether he speaks at all, for the optional comments on ordinary moves: `chattiness` is the
//    chance that he comments on a plain move (0 = silent, 1 = every move). Corners and big flips are
//    1.6x as likely to get a comment. Greetings, the start and the end of a game, passes, hints,
//    undo and the review verdicts are always spoken.

import type { Snapshot } from './api.ts';
import { POOLS, type PoolName } from './dialogues.ts';

export type Mood = 'idle' | 'think' | 'happy' | 'sad';
export interface Line {
  say: string;
  mood: Mood;
}
export type Rng = () => number;
export type Page = 'home' | 'setup-computer' | 'setup-two' | 'settings' | 'help';

export const DEALER_NAME = 'Orolleto';
/** Default chance that he comments on an ordinary move. */
export const DEFAULT_CHATTINESS = 0.55;
/** How many of his latest lines of one kind he will not repeat. */
export const DEFAULT_MEMORY = 8;

const CORNERS = [0, 7, 56, 63];
const SPECIAL_WEIGHT = 1.6;

/** A small deterministic random generator (mulberry32), so tests and the review can pin the choice. */
export function seededRng(seed: number): Rng {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
    let t = a;
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

export interface DealerOptions {
  chattiness?: number;
  rng?: Rng;
  memory?: number;
}

export class Dealer {
  readonly chattiness: number;
  private readonly rng: Rng;
  private readonly memory: number;
  private readonly recent = new Map<PoolName, string[]>();

  constructor(options: DealerOptions = {}) {
    this.chattiness = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, options.chattiness ?? DEFAULT_CHATTINESS));
    this.rng = options.rng ?? Math.random;
    this.memory = options.memory ?? DEFAULT_MEMORY;
  }

  /** A random line from `pool`, avoiding the ones used lately. */
  private say(pool: PoolName, mood: Mood): Line {
    const lines: readonly string[] = POOLS[pool];
    const recent = this.recent.get(pool) ?? [];
    const fresh = lines.filter((l) => !recent.includes(l));
    const choices = fresh.length ? fresh : lines;
    const say = choices[Math.min(choices.length - 1, Math.floor(this.rng() * choices.length))];
    this.recent.set(pool, [...recent, say].slice(-Math.min(this.memory, lines.length - 1)));
    return { say, mood };
  }

  /** True with probability chattiness × weight. */
  private chance(weight = 1): boolean {
    return this.rng() < this.chattiness * weight;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ pages

  /** What he says on a menu page. */
  page(page: Page): Line {
    const pool: PoolName =
      page === 'home' ? 'home' : page === 'setup-computer' ? 'setupComputer' : page === 'setup-two' ? 'setupTwo' : page;
    return this.say(pool, 'happy');
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ in a game

  /** The first words of a new game. */
  start(snap: Snapshot): Line {
    if (snap.mode.kind === 'two_players') return this.say('startTwo', 'happy');
    return this.say(snap.awaiting === 'computer' ? 'startComputerFirst' : 'startComputer', 'happy');
  }

  /** While the computer works out its move. */
  thinking(): Line {
    return this.say('thinking', 'think');
  }

  /**
   * His reaction when the game moves from `prev` to `next`, or null to stay quiet (always null in
   * two-player games, and for most ordinary moves unless he is feeling chatty).
   */
  afterMove(prev: Snapshot | null, next: Snapshot): Line | null {
    if (!prev || next.mode.kind !== 'vs_computer' || next.ply <= prev.ply || next.last_mov

// Orolleto: the dialogue pools and how he chooses from them. Run with:  npm test

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { test } from 'node:test';
import type { Snapshot } from './api.ts';
import { Dealer, seededRng, type Page } from './dealer.ts';
import { POOLS, POOL_SIZE, type PoolName } from './dialogues.ts';

const inPool = (pool: PoolName, say: string) => (POOLS[pool] as readonly string[]).includes(say);

/** A snapshot of a game against the computer (human = Black) in which `square` was just placed. */
function snap(opts: {
  ply: number;
  square: number | null;
  by?: 'black' | 'white';
  flips?: number;
  black?: number;
  white?: number;
  over?: 'human' | 'computer' | 'draw' | 'resigned';
  awaiting?: 'human' | 'computer';
}): Snapshot {
  const board = Array<number>(64).fill(0);
  if (opts.square !== null) board[opts.square] = opts.by === 'white' ? 2 : 1;
  const winner = opts.over === 'human' ? 'black' : opts.over === 'computer' || opts.over === 'resigned' ? 'white' : null;
  return {
    board,
    to_move: 'black',
    awaiting: opts.awaiting ?? 'human',
    legal: [],
    last_move: opts.square,
    flipped: Array.from({ length: opts.flips ?? 1 }, (_, i) => 20 + i),
    black_count: opts.black ?? 10,
    white_count: opts.white ?? 10,
    status: opts.over ? { state: 'over', winner, resigned: opts.over === 'resigned' } : { state: 'playing' },
    mode: { kind: 'vs_computer', difficulty: 2, human: 'black' },
    can_undo: false,
    ply: opts.ply,
    history: []
  };
}

const twoPlayer = (s: Snapshot): Snapshot => ({ ...s, mode: { kind: 'two_players' } });

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the pools

test('there is a huge pool of lines, and no pool repeats itself', () => {
  assert.ok(POOL_SIZE >= 380, `only ${POOL_SIZE} lines`);
  for (const [name, lines] of Object.entries(POOLS)) {
    assert.ok(lines.length >= 3, `${name} is too small`);
    assert.equal(new Set(lines).size, lines.length, `${name} has a duplicate line`);
    for (const line of lines) assert.ok(line.trim() === line && line.length > 2, `${name}: bad line "${line}"`);
  }
});

test('every menu page has its own lines', () => {
  const pages: Page[] = ['home', 'setup-computer', 'setup-two', 'settings', 'help'];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const d = new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(1) });
  for (const page of pages) {
    const line = d.page(page);
    assert.equal(line.mood, 'happy');
    assert.ok(!seen.has(line.say), 'a line was reused across pages');
    seen.add(line.say);
  }
  assert.ok(inPool('home', new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(2) }).page('home').say));
  assert.ok(inPool('setupComputer', new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(2) }).page('setup-computer').say));
  assert.ok(inPool('setupTwo', new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(2) }).page('setup-two').say));
  assert.ok(inPool('settings', new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(2) }).page('settings').say));
  assert.ok(inPool('help', new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(2) }).page('help').say));
});

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ choosing lines

test('the generator is deterministic for a seed', () => {
  const a = seededRng(42);
  const b = seededRng(42);
  assert.deepEqual([a(), a(), a()], [b(), b(), b()]);
  for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
    const x = a();
    assert.ok(x >= 0 && x < 1);
  }
});

test('he never repeats a line he said recently', () => {
  const d = new Dealer({ rng: seededRng(7), memory: 8 });
  const said: string[] = [];

  }

});

 * remark or a "thinking" line may replace it, so the bubble does not change with every move.

export const DEFAULT_HOLD_PLIES = 6;
/** How many of his latest lines of one kind he will not repeat. */""")
rep("""/** The one dealer the app talks through. */""","""/** What is on screen: a line, and the ply of the game it was said at. */
export interface Shown {
  line: Line;
  ply: number;
}

export const SILENT: Line = { say: '', mood: 'idle' };

/**
 * Decide what he shows after a game event. `candidate` is the line the dealer came up with (or null).
 * An ordinary candidate only replaces the current line once `hold` plies have passed (or if the
 * current line is empty or a "thinking" line); a special one always does; with no candidate the
 * current line stays, except that a stale "thinking" line is cleared when `clearTransient` is set.
 */
export function settle(shown: Shown, candidate: Line | null, ply: number, clearTransient = false, hold = DEFAULT_HOLD_PLIES): Shown {
  if (!candidate) return clearTransient && shown.line.transient ? { line: SILENT, ply } : shown;
  const held = ply - shown.ply < hold && ply >= shown.ply && !shown.line.transient && shown.line.say !== '';
  return candidate.special || !held ? { line: candidate, ply } : shown;
}

I fixed both. They're committed as 57b0262 and not pushed. The type-check, 65 unit tests and the browser game test pass.

Returning to the home screen - Cause: nothing in the app has an idle timer. I think the cause is the dev server. With launch.sh, it reloads the whole window when a file changes and when its connection drops after sleep. I have been editing files while you play, and a reload resets the app to home. I can't confirm that was your exact case. - Fix: the app now remembers which page you're on for the session. In the desktop app, a running game is picked up again from the engine after a reload. - Checked: I reloaded on the Settings page in Firefox and it stayed on Settings. I could not test the desktop game restore. It uses the same snapshot command the app already calls. - Limit: the web version keeps its game inside the page, so a reload there still ends the game.

His dialogue changing every move - Hold: a line now stays up for at least 6 half-moves (3 of your moves). Ordinary remarks and "thinking…" lines wait until then. - Exceptions: corners, big flips, passes, hints, undo and the end of the game still speak up at once. - Between moves: his bubble no longer goes blank, and the last line stays until there's something new. A stale "thinking…" line is cleared once he has moved. - Checked: over 14 moves in Firefox, the bubble changed 5 times instead of 14. - Settings: the hold (DEFAULT_HOLD_PLIES) and his chattiness are constants in ui/src/lib/dealer.ts. Tell me if you want either as a setting. - Review: I left the review alone. He still gives a line for each of your moves there, because each one gets its own verdict. If you want the review to hold lines too, say so.
